## R370 — The claim ledger: count what cannot be checked

**Annie's ruling, 2026-08-21.** `pnpm report:claim-ledger`.

**She has ruled R349's gap unclosable by any instrument, and the ledger exists because of that rather
than in spite of it.** *"Comparing a claim to a text is reading, and a machine doing it would be
substituting a string test for a judgement — which is the substitution that found thirty-two where I
found eight and cannot find the thirty-third."*

**So it counts; it does not check.** *"What can be built is not a check but a ledger. Which claims has
a reader compared with their text, when, and who. Then the population of unchecked claims is
countable, orderable by reachability, and visible as a number instead of being invisible as a kind.
That is the same move as the pin, one level up, and it is the only honest instrument for a property
whose only instrument is a person."*

**SCOPED ACROSS THE WHOLE CLASS, not the 61** — hers: *"curation notes, band justifications,
misconception descriptions against their tagged items, walk scripts against their cited lines. Every
one of those is a claim about a text."*

| kind | total | compared | UNREAD & REACHABLE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| walk script vs cited lines | 705 | 0 | 340 |
| misconception vs tagged items | 278 | 0 | 100 |
| flag reason | 61 | 0 | 1 |
| band justification | 27 | 0 | 1 |
| curation note | 21 | 0 | 1 |
| **TOTAL** | **1092** | **0** | **443** |

**The 61 were 6% of it.** The read is ordered by reachability and starts at
`en-plausible-not-stated#description` — **209 LIVE options carry it**, and nobody has compared its
description with a single one of them.

**A ledger row is written by a person who has read both, never by the script.** The claims population
must not be empty (`requirePopulation`); the LEDGER legitimately is, on day one, and says so with its
reason (`declareMayBeEmpty`) — an empty ledger is a true report of an unstarted read, which is the
number this exists to make visible.

## R372 — The strike test: a reason is load-bearing where the verdict falls without it

**Annie's ruling, 2026-08-21. Registered as hers.**

R349 asked whether a factual claim inside a flag's reason is part of the JUDGEMENT or part of the
EXPLANATION, and reported that the two cases pointed opposite ways. **They do not. The test is a
procedure rather than a taxonomy.**

**A claim is load-bearing if striking it leaves the verdict unsupported. So strike it and read what
remains.**

- Strike *the rabbit is unhurt* → *brief comic rudeness, the tone farcical rather than cruel.* The
  verdict stands. **The claim was OFFERED as load-bearing and is not.**
- Strike *never named* → *never used, only reached for, and the pressure that makes Priya speak.* The
  verdict stands.

**Both are explanation. Both survive. The cases point the same way once the test is applied rather
than the phrasing compared** — which is the correction to my own report, and the reason a procedure
beats a taxonomy: I compared how the two clauses were WORDED and got two answers.

**AND THE TEST EARNS ITS KEEP ON THE CASE IT FAILS.** *"If striking a claim leaves nothing, the
verdict rested on that claim and correcting it reopens the verdict. If striking EVERY claim leaves the
verdict standing, the reason was decorative and the verdict rests on the judge's unstated axis, which
is the actual disease. The strike test detects both, and it is the one thing on this list a reader can
apply in seconds."*

STAFF screen.** No child path reads it. That is either rationale, or **an unwired hint — content
authored for a child, gated for a child, and never plumbed to one.** **Those are opposite conclusions
and nothing in the store distinguishes them.** It is `walkScript` before Walk was built, and it has
gone unnoticed precisely because the gate has been treating it as served all along.

**THREE STATES, NOT TWO**, which is why the question cannot be answered by a served/not-served split:
**RATIONALE** (provenance and workflow — `hintAuthority`, `walkScriptBatch`); **STRUCTURE**
(machine-readable declarations — `answerShape`, `exemptFrom`, where a reading-age cap is close to
meaningless); and **AUTHORED-FOR-A-CHILD BUT UNSERVED** (`hintCore`), **where gating is right even
though nothing serves it, because the day something does, the gate is what stands between the
authoring and the child.**

The served column is a NAME SCAN and stated as a proxy (R60): it can over-report a name in a comment
and under-report a field read through a spread.

## R380 — The ban list's scope, narrowed, with the schema check shipped in the same act

**Annie's ruling, 2026-08-21.** `packages/core/src/ban-list-scope.ts`, `pnpm check:declaration-schema`.

**In scope: the served paths and class 3. Nothing else.**

**Provenance and workflow are OUT, with `correctionOf` as the decisive case** — *"a field whose job is
to record a fault will contain the fault, so a gate banning the word from the field that records it
makes the record impossible."* Not a tolerance: a contradiction. The field cannot do its job and pass.

**Machine declarations are OUT, under a rider that OUTRANKS the ruling: removing a check must not
leave a field with none.** *"A field nobody checks is how the word cap ran for a month."* So
`check:declaration-schema` ships in the same commit and asks what actually applies to a declaration —
**is the shape valid, does the declared span exist in a text on its own container, does the exemption
name a rule that exists** (register-derived, never hand-listed). **28 faults on first run**, all one
class: declarations resolving to no text on their container.

**`hintCore` is class 3 whatever Lookup 1 says** — authored for a child, gated as child-facing, in
scope **because the day something serves it the gate is what stands between the authoring and the
child.** `walkScript`'s case exactly, one field over, invisible because the gate treated it as served.

**Baselined before and after (R149): NOTHING MOVED.** No existing failure sat on an out-of-scope
field, so the narrowing is correct and currently unexercised — an outcome, not a vindication (R62).

**AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT PRODUCED THE RULING WAS ITSELF WRONG, CORRECTED HERE.** It reported **35
screened paths**; the true figure is **25**. It called `textsFrom` on the explanation object, which is
what the gate does for the stem and for option content **but NOT for the explanation**, whose loop
reads three named fields. So `walkScriptBatch`, `walkScriptStatus`, `hintAuthority` and
`hintAuthoredBy` — 678 values, four of the eleven in the not-served column — **were reported as
screened when the gate has never touched them.** R41's fault: a verifier re-deriving the property
instead of calling the family's own code, in evidence that went to a reviewer for a ruling.

## R384 — `hintCore` is a review job, not a plumbing job, and the number says which

**2026-08-21, costed and not built.** 373 authored values wired to nothing (R379).

| | |
|---|---:|
| items carrying a `hintCore` | 373 |
| of those LIVE | **43** |
| LIVE ones whose wrong options route to a library hint | **43** |
| LIVE ones with **no** library hint behind any wrong option | **0** |
| library hints reachable from LIVE items | 28 |
| reached **only** from items carrying a `hintCore` | **28** |

**THE FALLBACK POPULATION IS EMPTY.** A plumbing job is one where some items have their own hint and
others fall through; **that case does not exist here.** Wherever an item hint is reachable, a library
hint is already there. So the build is one conditional in `orchestrator.ts:940` and it **displaces all
28 reachable library hints at once** — every one approved text, with no partial rollout.

**The two hints are not competing versions of one thing, which is why the store cannot decide it.**
`ENG-003-A-PU-02` serves *"If the SPOKEN words are the question, the mark lives inside the speech
marks"* while its own unread hint reads **"Does your voice go up at the end? Then it needs a question
mark."** **The first names the rule; the second names what the child can do.** Two different teaching
acts, and which belongs at a miss is a judgement about teaching, not about plumbing.

**And it compounds: 330 of the 373 sit on DRAFT items.** Deciding now costs one ruling; deciding after
the DRAFT backlog publishes costs the same ruling against eight times the content.

## R385 — Three names agreed to and not held; none is reconciled

**David, 2026-08-21.** Cowork holds **no `quotedFieldVerdict`, no `isSuperseded`, and 29 gates rather
than 25.** Each time **the shape was right and the name was wrong.**

**A name agreed to but not held produces a register entry pointing at nothing** — the same fault as an
authority string citing a filename that never existed on either side. The entry reads as a shared
mechanism; the grep on the other store returns empty; and the reader concludes the mechanism is
missing rather than differently named.

**None is reconciled, and that is the ruling rather than a deferral.** Renaming either side to match
would make one store's code answer to the other store's vocabulary, and **the shapes already agree —
it is only the labels that do not.** What must stop is citing a name across the boundary as though it
were held there.

**The discipline that follows: a cross-store citation names the SHAPE and the store.** *"the guard
that skips archival keys on the walk, called `isSuperseded` here"* survives a rename on either side;
*"`isSuperseded`"* does not. This is R178's look-it-up rule at a boundary where the lookup cannot be
performed — **the register can only be checked against the store that wrote it.**

## R388 — `hintCore` plumbed with its gate in the same act: read serves, unread does not

**Annie's ruling, 2026-08-21.** `packages/core/src/item-hint.ts`, wired at `orchestrator.ts:940`.

**An item hint serves ONLY if a named reviewer has read it; otherwise the library hint serves exactly
as today.** 7 of 373 carry `hintAuthoredBy` **and** `hintAuthority`; **none of the other 366 reaches a
child on the strength of being plumbed.** Nothing regresses, nothing unread ships, and **the backlog
drains by READING rather than by outage — the pin applied at the moment a field is wired rather than
after.**

**BOTH a name and an authority are required.** A bare name is an assertion; a bare citation is
unattributed. That is R94's conflation moved into a serving decision, where it would put an agent's
words in front of a child under a reviewer's authority.

**WHERE IT SERVES, IT SUPERSEDES — one hint, not two.** Her reason: *an item hint is authored knowing
that item's actual options and actual trap, while a library hint must be true of every carrier.* A
child who has just got something wrong is least able to read two things.

**THE GATE IS THE WIRING, NOT A STEP AFTER IT.** Plumbing first and gating later would put 366 unread
strings one deploy away from a child, and the gap between those two commits is exactly where this
content escapes.

**Today it changes nothing a child sees, and that is by construction rather than by luck: all seven
attested items are DRAFT.** The 43 LIVE hint-carrying items continue to serve the library hint. The
wiring begins to matter on the day those seven publish — **which is the correct order, since the
alternative is a rule that arrives after the content it governs.** 8 tests.

## R389 — Cowork's reachability test applied here: `stem.text` and `stem.prompt` are EARNED, the rest are INFERRED

**Cowork's test, 2026-08-21: does a reachability entry NAME WHO ESTABLISHED IT, or argue from
likeness? The second is a guess wearing a declaration's clothes.**

**Applied to my own entries, and it does not flatter them.** `SERVED_PATHS` was built from a NAME SCAN
over the child surface — a grep for each leaf name. **That is inference, and 23 paths were declared on
it.** The column heading said *"in scope beyond argument"*, which is the exact sentence Cowork warns
about.

**EARNED, traced this turn to a render:**
- **`stem.text` and `stem.prompt`** — `play-runner.tsx:741` calls `stemText()`, which reads
  `stem.text` then `stem.prompt` at `engines/shared.ts:45-47` and **THROWS if neither is present**.
  A named function on a child path that refuses rather than defaulting: reachability established by
  reading the code, not by resemblance.
- **`option.content.value`** — `engines/errorspot.tsx:49` projects `content.value` into `raw` and
  renders it at `:68`, `:134`, `:150`.
- **`explanation.walkScript`** — the Walk mode dispatcher, built and traced.
- **`explanation.hintCore`** — traced to a STAFF screen only, which is how the unwiring was found.

**INFERRED, and now labelled as such:** the remaining ~19 paths in `SERVED_PATHS` — `stem.sentence`,
`stem.code.*`, `stem.question`, `stem.wordWithGap`, `stem.techniqueKey`, `stem.operands.kind`,
`stem.passageRef`, the `quotes[]` fields, `option.label`, `explanation.note`. **Every one rests on a
grep hit and none names who established it.**

**And the test earns its keep on the entry it caught: `hintCore` was declared REACHABLE from
resemblance to `walkScript`** — the item-level form of the same string — and it is not served at all.
**A likeness argument produced a declaration that was exactly wrong**, on 373 values, for as long as
anyone had been reading it.

**THE RULE: a reachability entry names the reader and the path, or it is marked INFERRED.** Not
removed — an inferred entry is still the best guess available — but never presented as a state. And
**a store does not declare reachability for a surface it cannot observe**: that is a claim, not a
state, and it is why this list is mine to hold rather than Cowork's.

## R391 — `en-contradicted-by-the-text` drafted; and the eight retags proposed, none assigned

**Annie's twenty-fourth return, 2026-08-21. Drafted for approval; nothing written to the library.**
Staged: `EN-CONTRADICTED-BY-THE-TEXT-DRAFT.md`, `a6c8d3e43d231f6a…`.

**Description, her scope verbatim:** *chooses an option the passage explicitly denies, rather than one
it merely fails to support.*

**Three child-hint drafts, all three passing the gate, with A recommended:** *"The passage says the
opposite. Go back and find the line that disagrees."* Her reason is the argument for it — **a child
who picks one of these has missed a line, not invented one** — and A tells her a line exists and sends
her to it. B (*contradicted by it*) is the most precise and the most abstract, at the moment she is
least able to follow an abstraction. C risks sending her back to the options rather than the passage.

**WHAT A DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SAY.** `en-plausible-not-stated` ends *"point to the line that proves
it"* — go and find evidence. **For this error the evidence is already there and says the opposite**, so
an instruction to hunt for support is the same wrong turn one step later. **A hint written for one
error is not neutral on the other; it is actively wrong on it**, which is why this leads the queue
rather than sitting in it.

**Her finding, restated because it is about a child and not a taxonomy:** on seven of twenty-seven
carriers the most carried hint in the product sends a child hunting for a line that **cannot exist**,
and when she fails to find it **she learns the instruction does not work** rather than that her answer
was unsupported.

**The eight retags are PROPOSED WITH THEIR REASONING, never assigned.** Five vocabulary split
dominant-sense (*carol* as a church bell, *stern* as a cushioned seat — the everyday sense displacing
the one on the page) from neighbouring-sense (*made fast* as waving — an adjacent sense of the same
phrase). **`en-vocab-form-lookalike` is proposed for none of the five**, and the reason is stated:
nothing here turns on a word that merely LOOKS like another, and offering a tag where it does not
apply is how a family of tags stops meaning anything.

**`ENG-001-WIW-22` is flagged as the least confident, in her own direction.** She noted it contradicts
the page — the animals ARE called Mole and Rat — so it has a foot in group three. It is proposed as
`en-technique-device-confusion` because the STEM asks what the writer is doing; **if she reads it the
other way it joins the seven and becomes eight.** Naming my own weakest proposal is cheaper than her

## R393 — Her form-lookalike paragraph, rated above the assignments it governs

**Annie, 2026-08-21, and she rates it higher than the five calls it decided.**

> Nothing here turns on a word that merely looks like another, and offering a tag where it does not
> apply is how a family of tags stops meaning anything.

**The failure it names is not a wrong tag — it is a tag family losing its edges.** `dominant-sense`,
`neighbouring-sense` and `form-lookalike` only mean anything while each is refused where it does not
fit. **Offer the third whenever the first two are uncertain and all three collapse into "vocabulary
error"**, at which point the library has one tag wearing three names and no way to notice.

**It generalises past vocabulary and past this store.** Any tag family with adjacent members degrades
by generosity rather than by error: nobody assigns a badly wrong tag, they assign a nearly-right one,
and the family's boundaries erode from the inside where no check is looking. **`check:authority-shape`
screens who says a thing and `check:declaration-schema` screens whether a declaration resolves;
nothing screens whether a taxonomy still distinguishes.**

**And her boundary rule, which decided WIW-22:** where an option is both a wrong account of the device
and false on the page, **the STEM decides** — it asks what the writer is doing, so the technique entry
holds. I had flagged WIW-22 as my least confident and offered that it might become an eighth
contradicted item; **she ruled the boundary rather than the instance**, which is why it settles the
next one as well.

## R395 — ACTIVE-BUT-UNREACHED: the hint gate is a state, not a fact about today

**Annie, 2026-08-21.** `pnpm check:hint-gate-state`. **A gate that is correct and does nothing reads
identically to a gate that is working.**

R388 serves an item hint only where a named reviewer has read it. **It serves none — and the rule
refuses nothing.** The read hints and the reachable items are **disjoint populations**: her seven sit
on two spelling-spot and five cloze items, **and neither type has a door.** So the gate wires a field,
finds no read hint on any reachable item, and falls through to the library hint on all nine.

**Recorded as a STATE with its reason**: `ACTIVE-BUT-UNREACHED`, flipping to `ACTIVE-AND-SERVING` the
moment a read hint lands on a reachable item — by a ruling on one of the nine, or by a door opening
for spelling-spot or cloze. **Both are outstanding work and the check names them**, so *"no item hint
served"* can never be read as *"the gate declined to serve one"*.

**The nine are sent verbatim for her ruling** — `NINE-PUNCT-HINTS-FOR-RULING.md`, `a07fc1c2c72f70f8…`
— each with its item, its unread hint, and the library hint a child sees today. **Not objecting to
the rest is not an approval**: no id, no string quoted, no artefact cited is the shape she refused
from both stores this week, and thirty-four read with seven replaced leaves twenty-seven unruled
rather than approved.

**And the check's own first run printed five item ids as though they were five TYPES** —
`ENG-003-A-CZ-B3` has no trailing number to strip, so a lazy regex reported the population's shape
wrongly in the line whose entire job is naming it. Fixed to match the type.

## R396 — Classifying by the question rather than by the error

**Annie, 2026-08-21, and it is measure-the-property-under-test arriving in taxonomy.**

**The stem's type is not the error's type.** I proposed polysemy tags for three options that are not a
sense of their word at all, **because the stems were vocabulary stems** — I classified by what the
question asks rather than by what the child did wrong.

**`ENG-001-WIW-11` proves it from the other side**: a vocabulary stem whose distractor is a **motive
invention**, correctly staying under `en-plausible-not-stated`. **The two errors run in opposite
directions from the same premise** — a vocabulary stem can carry a non-vocabulary error, and a
vocabulary error can appear on a stem that is not asking about a word. `en-vocab-dominant-sense`'s own
scope note already said so: *scoped to the ERROR, not to vocabulary items.*

**A tag names what went wrong in the child's head, never what the question was about.**

## R397 — A citation is a second and independent assertion

**Annie, 2026-08-21, and she owns the wrong return number as hers rather than the guard's.**

The apply script located her hint **in her file** and aborted: the string was right, **the citation was
wrong** — the twenty-fourth return, where the hint is authored in the twenty-fifth.

**The whole value of the form is having two claims that can disagree.** A retyped value is ONE claim
and can only be checked against itself. A value plus its citation is TWO, and **the disagreement is
the finding whichever of them turns out to be wrong** — here the citation, once the string that
disagreed with it was located.

**So a citation is not decoration on a value and not provenance for the record.** It is a second
measurement of the same fact, and its worth is exactly that it can fail independently.

## R398 — A hint is written for a population, so its strongest claim must be true of its weakest member

**Annie's hint rule, 2026-08-21, in its practical form.**

> **Write it after reading the carriers, or write it weak enough to survive the ones you have not
> read.**

My three drafts each said more than the population supports. *"Says the opposite"* **overstates on
PR-09**, where the wasps have not moved away but **multiplied in the same square of air** — different,
not opposite. *"The line that disagrees"* leaves the referent implicit **for the reader least able to
supply one.** Each was accurate on the carriers I had in mind and wrong on the one I had not read.

**Her own words on the choice she made: worse prose and truer.** *"One line in the passage says
something different"* is flatter than any of the three and true on all six. **A hint is not a sentence
about an error; it is a sentence that must hold across every child who meets it**, and the strongest
phrasing is reliably the one that fails first.

## R407 — The sweep: one instance, and it is the one already known

**David, 2026-08-21.** `pnpm check:reasoning-premises`. **32 returns swept against every authored
wording and its date. One finding: the twenty-fourth**, already confirmed.

**The test:** a return quotes a string as being IN FORCE; if that string is an authored wording from
an EARLIER return that had not landed, **the premise was false when written.**

**Her twenty-fourth quotes her own seventeenth-return wording as the hint in force and reasons from
it about seven carriers.** It had never been written.

**AND THE REASONING SURVIVES, WHICH IS THE DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING.** Her finding rested on **what
the hint ASKS** — it sends a child hunting for a line that cannot exist, and she learns the
instruction does not work rather than that her answer was unsupported. **Both strings ask it.**
*"Point to the line that proves it"* sends her hunting exactly as *"find the line that proves it"*
does. **A conclusion resting on the ERROR survives a false premise; one resting on the WORDING may
not** — and hers rested on the error.

**Its bound, because a clean sweep is worth exactly what its method is worth** (R60): it sees a
quoted string matchable to the authored set, in her quotation shapes. **A premise quoted correctly,
paraphrased, or reasoned from without being quoted is invisible.** *No further instance FOUND*, never
*no further instance EXISTS*.

**And the reason she could not have caught it herself belongs in the entry:** she has no way to check
whether the premise under her own conclusion was ever true. **She wrote a wording, read it back in her
own record, and the record was right about what she decided and silent about whether it took effect.**
Only this store can see the difference, and until today nothing here was looking either.

one a reader assumes: ABSENT reads as *nobody applied it*, when it may mean *nobody looked there*.

legitimately occurs** — the first run flagged VR letter-series items where **N is a genuine letter of
the alphabet**, a real option value with a walk script correctly naming it. **Too wide and too narrow

option.

## R415 — An extractor that reads one of a source's shapes reports A population, not THE population

**David, 2026-08-21, and it is a shape rather than an instance.**

it does not recognise FAILS rather than yields nothing.** Silence on an unrecognised shape is the
same fault as `?? []` on a failed parse (R173) — a reader that cannot parse, reporting a fact about
the content.

`` - `entry-id`, replacing *old*: **new** ``: missing it lost the id too, which is why the first pass
had wordings it could not place. **A shape is not a formatting variant; it is a different record with
different fields.**

## R427 — Target-dropping is the live defect, and it is in the CHECK

**Annie's disjunction, 2026-08-21, and the second branch is the true one.**

Her inline form carries the target at the head of the line:
`` - `en-attribute-transfer`, replacing *old*: **new** ``. **So format-blindness cannot explain the
orphan — the id was right there.**

**The check's inline pattern is `/replacing\s+\*[^*]+\*\s*:\s*\*\*(.+?)\*\*/gms` — ONE capture group,
the authored wording. It never captures the backticked id at all.** Every inline amendment reaches
`check:amendments-landed` **with its target discarded**, by construction.

**The apply script uses a DIFFERENT regex that DOES capture the id** — which is why it placed six
targets the check could not. **Two regexes over one source, disagreeing about what a record contains.**

**So the two defects are separate and only one is fixed.** Format-blindness (R415) lost whole returns
and is repaired. **Target-dropping is LIVE in the check**, and it produces orphans **that look like
author error** — which is exactly what `en-attribute-transfer` looked like for three counts, until she
named its target in a sentence.

**The distinction matters because they fail differently: format-blindness under-reports and looks like
a clean return; target-dropping reports the row and misattributes its cause to the author.** The
second is worse and it is the one still standing.

## R429 — One reader of a return, because two parsers over one format will disagree

**Annie, 2026-08-21: the two regexes are the finding rather than the bug.**

`check:amendments-landed` and `apply-all-unlanded` both read her returns and **disagreed about what a
record contains** — the apply script captured the target id, the check discarded it **by
construction**. So every inline amendment the check ever reported was reported **without a target**,
and the disagreement made a correctly-formed amendment look like author error for three counts.

**`scripts/lib/return-amendments.ts` is now the one reader, imported by both.** The shapes are
DECLARED and **printed on every run**:

```
INLINE_WITH_TARGET: - `entry-id`, replacing *old text*: **new text**
LABELLED:           - authored: **new text**   (no target carried)
```

**A richer record supersedes the same wording read by a poorer shape**, so an amendment carrying its
target is never demoted to an orphan by the order the patterns happen to run in.

**AND THE TARGET NOW SCOPES THE MATCH.** Comparing a wording against the whole store answers *"does
this string exist somewhere"*; comparing it against **its own row** answers *"did this amendment
reach its target"*. The first is the weaker question, and a wording that happened to match another
entry would have reported a landing on the wrong row.

**Re-run over the whole population: 33 wordings, 33 landed, 0 absent.** The number did not move — but
**what it means did**: previously *these strings exist somewhere in the store*, now *each amendment is
on the row it names*. The population was right and the property being measured was not.

## R431 — Her description and her hint on the entry; the proposal's becomes a boundary clause

**Annie's twenty-fifth return, applied 2026-08-21.** `en-contradicted-by-the-text` carries **her**
description and **her** hint, both already in place. **The proposal's wording is now the entry's FIRST
BOUNDARY CLAUSE** rather than a competing description:

> *Distinguished from a plausible option the passage never states: here the passage states the
> contrary. Negation-dropped loses a WORD; this loses a CLAIM, and the option may share no wording
> with the line that refutes it.*

**Her reason is a rule about descriptions: a description that argues its own boundaries is doing two
jobs.** One says what the error IS; the other says what it is NOT. Collapsing them makes a description
that reads as a definition and behaves as a comparison, and a tagger reaching for it gets both at once
without knowing which is load-bearing.

**AND THE PROVENANCE IS RECORDED SO NOBODY RECONCILES IT LATER BY PICKING THE NEWER FILE.** The
proposal predates her ruling crossing; **file order would resolve it backwards**, which is exactly how
a superseded wording gets restored by someone tidying.

## R432 — The boundary clause settled a case its own author called contestable

**Annie, 2026-08-21.** `ENG-005-BB-06` option A — *"He was not frightened by the falling tree."* —
moves from `en-relation-word-flipped` to **`en-negation-dropped`**.

**claim**, and the option may share no wording with the line that refutes it. Here **the option reads
*not frightened* and so does the line** — a dropped word, not a denied claim.

**A boundary clause good enough to settle a case its author called contestable is a well-drawn
boundary**, and that is the test worth keeping: not whether a boundary sounds principled, but whether
it decides an instance the person who wrote it could not.

`ENG-004-AGG-01` option B — *"He noticed her red hair and freckled face."* — confirmed under
`en-wrong-scope-retrieval` by her general rule; it was already there.

## R433 — The dual-mechanism rule, with its fallback

**Annie, 2026-08-21.** Where a distractor pulls by two mechanisms, tag the one the child's error
actually turns on. **And the fallback is the part that matters: if neither hint accounts for the pull,
the distractor needs an entry that does.**

**That fallback is how `en-contradicted-by-the-text` came to exist.** Seven options pulled by something
neither `en-plausible-not-stated` nor any neighbouring tag explained, and the resolution was **a new
entry rather than a better argument for an existing one.**

**The rule refuses the comfortable move**: choosing the least-wrong existing tag is always available
and always looks like a decision. **A tag that does not account for the pull is a tag that will send
the child somewhere useless**, and the library growing is the correct outcome rather than a failure of
economy.

## R440 — Why the containment check missed four of five: it was right about all of them

**Not a tightening opportunity. This is the population the check DECLARED unreachable, arriving with
names.**

- `melancholy` — **sadness / sad**: same.
- `notorious` — **famous / infamous**: same, and the affix is a prefix.
- `vague` — **not clear / unclear**: **the paraphrase band**, which no containment test reaches at all.

**Only `exhausted` was a true containment case, and it was invisible for a different reason: timing.**

than a limit discovered by failure**, and it is the argument for stating a bound rather than reporting
a number.

## R443 — Two instruments over one queue: 364/54 against 325/58

**Both ran. They disagree, and neither is wrong.**

staged, 58 crossed.**

the number of correctly-delivered artefacts — **so the queue looks worse the more carefully things are
delivered.** And it reads acknowledgement from **filenames mentioned in anything inbound**, which a
message can do without the file ever being opened.

**The diff counts distinct CONTENT and matches on VALUE**, against a manifest the receiver computed.
Only one of these is a statement about her disk.

**AND MY OWN HAND COUNT REACHED 58 BY THE WEAKER METHOD.** Reporting that as agreement with the digest
diff would have retired the question — **the same number by a weaker method is not a second
measurement**, and two instruments agreeing is only evidence when they are measuring the same thing.
R173's confirming-result fault, avoided by noticing the methods differed rather than by the numbers
disagreeing.

## R447 — What the WIDER reopening would cost, since obedient and exhausted both deserved it

**Her generalisation, costed and NOT built.** A key change also moves:

  `obedient` and `exhausted` are PROVISIONAL against an unverified direction (R336). **A key change
  invalidates a direction judgement that was made about the old key.**
- **the DISTRACTOR SET's fairness** — the remaining options were authored to be wrong against the OLD
  key. `tired` became a free string when `worn out` replaced it, and is now the textbook wrong-strength
  distractor nobody has ruled on (D1).
- **any HINT that names the answer** — an item hint written for the old key can describe a route to a
  word that is no longer correct.

**The cost is not the checks; it is that three of the four have no automatic test.** The card
comparison is mechanical. **Direction needs a frequency source that is UNESTABLISHED. Distractor
fairness is a reviewer judgement. A hint naming the answer is the claim-against-text class R349 ruled
unclosable by any instrument.**

**So a full reopening on key change is ONE machine check and THREE reviewer reads**, and building it
as an automatic trigger would produce a queue of reviewer work with no reviewer attached — **which is
the conditional-flag backlog again, generated automatically.** Recorded as the cost; the ruling is
hers.

## R450 — A key change reopens the item; serving continues; publication blocks until signed

**Annie's ruling, 2026-08-21, and it reuses the conditional-flag schema unchanged.**

**Blocking SERVING would keep a faulty key in front of children while the repair waited** — worse than
the fault the block prevents. So: **the item keeps serving, and publication of anything on that item
blocks until the reopening is signed.**

**The reopening record takes `owner`, `reviewBy`, `state`, and is REFUSED AT AUTHORING without an
owner** — the same three fields and the same refusal as R368, **so there is no new machinery.**

**THE SHAPE THAT MAKES IT WORK: three judgements become ONE reopening with ONE owner, rather than
three queues with none.** R447 costed the wider version as one machine check and three reviewer reads
and warned it would generate a reviewer queue with nobody attached. **Her ruling dissolves that by
making the reopening the unit** — direction, distractor fairness and hint-names-the-answer are things
the owner reads, not things that each spawn a row.

**The narrow card check stays automatic because it has an answer.** A check with a machine answer
runs; a judgement without one gets an owner and a date. **That is the line, and it is a property of
the question rather than of the effort.**

path.** Her seventeenth return is the document that authored the `en-plausible-not-stated` wording
whose non-landing took a week to find; **it is now on her disk as an artefact this store cannot

**Recording rather than repairing is her call and it is the right one**: repairing it means inventing
a provenance record for a route that had none, which would be a reconstruction wearing a receipt's
clothes.

## R452 — Luck is not corroboration

**Annie's rule, 2026-08-21.** Two methods agreeing is evidence **only if both are independent and
sound**. A weak method landing on a strong method's answer is **one measurement and one coincidence**.

**The instance: my hand count reached 58 by filename matching; the digest diff reached 58 by value.**
Reporting the agreement would have retired the question, and **the weaker number was not made better
by matching the better one.**

**IT IS INVISIBLE BECAUSE AGREEMENT LOOKS LIKE CONFIRMATION FROM EITHER SIDE.** Nothing in the output
distinguishes two sound instruments concurring from one sound instrument and one that happened to
land nearby — **the numbers are identical and only the methods differ.** So the check is on the
METHODS, before the numbers are compared, and it cannot be done afterwards.

**A number that agrees with a better number is not thereby a better number.**

## R455 — The write and the hold-lift are two acts, and only one of them is mine

**The fourteen on held cards: eight headwords, redrafts already approved in her eighteenth return.**

**THE WRITE** is one act and mechanical: apply the eight approved redrafts to their `definitionChild`
fields, read from her return with its digest as authority, each asserted by reading the row back —
the same path as the five cards in R439, which ran clean. **The card texts above are the pre-redraft
values, so the write has somewhere to land and the leak closes with it.**

**THE HOLD-LIFT is a separate act and it is HERS.** A hold is a reviewer state; lifting it is a
judgement that the reason for the hold is gone. **Writing the redraft removes the fault; it does not
remove the hold, and nothing here should treat one as implying the other** — that is the two-way
editing line in a different field, and a store that lifts its own holds when it thinks it has fixed
the cause has no hold mechanism at all.

**So: two acts, in order, with the second not mine.** The write can proceed now. The lift waits on her
saying the redrafts satisfy what the hold was for.

**And the three LIVE ones are a THIRD act, in the opposite direction.** `swift`, `tidy`, `timid` do
not need a lift — **they need the hold she ruled to actually reach them.** She named them held; the
store has them serving. **Carrying them "into the lift" is exactly backwards**, and it is the
correction R454 forces: they are not held-and-harmless, they are leaking-and-live.

## R473 — The off-by-one side is NOT chosen; the collision is one generation away

**Her cheap question, answered from the generator rather than assumed.**

```
'vr-letter-series-off-by-one': (op) => [vrLetterOf(op.answer + 1), vrLetterOf(op.answer - 1)]
'vr-letter-series-step-repeat': (op) => [vrLetterOf(op.answer + op.step)]
```

**`off-by-one` returns BOTH sides as candidates.** `step-repeat` returns `answer + step`. **On a
step-1 series that is `answer + 1` — which is one of off-by-one's two candidates.**

**So the two tags CAN produce the identical letter, and the five observed step-1 items avoid it only
because the selector happened to take `answer − 1`.** That is a fact about selection, not about
design: **nothing in the generator prevents it.**

**Her condition applies: it happens to, so the assert is owed even though the population is currently
zero.** The invariant is *on a step-1 series, `off-by-one` must not select `answer + step`* — and the
zero it will report needs its before-count and its reason on its face (R421), because a check that has
never fired over a fault that has never occurred is indistinguishable from one pointed at nothing.

invalidating the file.

**42 approved-content snapshots are in the inbound folder and EVERY ONE has a later return** — the
oldest carrying 43. `misconceptionimport (1).json` (71 rows, 1 August), `WSREDRAFT1.json`, eight

**AND THIS ONE RAN IN THE SAFE DIRECTION, WHICH IS WHAT MADE IT COMFORTABLE TO ACCEPT.** *"The hold is

## R495 — A VALUE CARRIES THE PROPERTY THAT DECIDES HOW IT MAY BE USED

**Annie's rule, 2026-08-21, registered ABOVE its four instances so the next one is a fifth instance
rather than a new rule.**

> **An approval carries WHERE THE STRING WAS READ.
> A number carries WHAT IT COUNTED.
> An assert carries HOW ITS INVARIANT WAS DERIVED.
> A match carries WHAT KIND OF MATCH IT IS.**

**Each is the same rule.** A bare value is usable in ways its provenance forbids, and **the property
that forbids them is known at the moment the value is produced and discarded there.** Every instance
below cost a wrong number reported as a measurement.

| instance | the property dropped | what it cost |
|---|---|---|
| **approval** (R25, R397) | where the string was read | a hint retyped from memory; a citation naming the wrong return |
| **number** (R475, R494) | what it counted | *"leaks nothing"* over a DRAFT-only filter; four clean cards read as four measurements |
| **assert** (R490, R492) | how the invariant was derived | *"off-by-one is the lower side"* — read off results, false, would have fired constantly |
| **match** (R495, below) | what kind of match | seven still-read snapshots that were three, then one |

**THE NEXT ONE IS A FIFTH INSTANCE.** The rule is not *"record provenance"* — it is that **the value

## R512 — An artefact that offers a READING of an option carries the set too

**Her correction, and it is the harder half.** **She did not misjudge the option — she RATIFIED A
READING of it.** The carriers document called it *a claim about narrative technique*; she adopted that
and built on it **without asking what the key was.**

**So the rule reaches further than artefacts that ASK for a verdict. An artefact that OFFERS a reading
of an option carries the option set too.**

**A READING ARRIVES ALREADY ARGUED, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES ACCEPTING ONE CHEAPER TO DO WRONG THAN FORMING
ONE.** A verdict request presents an option and asks; a reading presents an option *and the conclusion*,
and the reader's work is reduced to assent or objection. **The evidence needed to object is exactly
what the artefact left out.**

**Four artefacts are in this class**: `export-terminal-over-ceiling`, `export-vr-audit-sample`,
`export-vr-pattern-sample`, `export-vr04-forty-ranks`. **And the carriers document that caused this was
not among them** — it was hand-written, which is where the class is least visible.

## R513 — The check's FLOOR is the finding, and it goes on the artefact's face

**944 artefacts, 2 key-claims, 2 wrong. THAT IS NOT A RATE.**

**It says quoting a carrier's key is a practice almost nobody follows** — and **the one file that
followed it got both wrong**, so **the fault was concentrated rather than distributed.** A hundred
percent failure over a population of two is a statement about the population, not about the practice.

**The check reaches a proposal that QUOTES a key. It cannot reach one that CHARACTERISES a carrier in
prose — which is what a proposal normally does.** The carriers document that caused R503 characterised
rather than quoted, and would not be caught by this check today.

**Worth having and not coverage, and it must say so on its face** — a check whose result is *2 of 2
wrong* will be read as thorough unless the denominator's smallness is printed beside it.

## R514 — A pattern written for one serialisation fails silently on another

**Her new face of the match rule (R495), and it is the same family as direction-never-asked and
footnotes-counted-as-readers.**

**A single pattern over a mixed population covers ONE FORMAT while reporting on ALL of them.** My
key-claim pattern demanded a quote immediately after `key:`. In markdown that is `key: "…"`; **in JSON
it is `key: \"…\"` and the next character is a backslash.** It screened 944 artefacts across both
formats and matched **zero**.

**A MATCH NOT CARRYING ITS KIND, WHERE THE KIND IS THE FORMAT.** The scan knew which files were JSON
and which were markdown, and threw that away before matching — exactly as the reader scan knew which
matches were imports and which were footnotes.

**And it was caught by `requirePopulation`, not by the pattern.** The zero was refused before it
became a number, which is the only reason this is a register entry rather than a clean result.

**The pattern is now the finding rather than the instance.** Three in two turns: a quote after `key:`

that was a footnote. **Each was a single pattern over a population that varies in a dimension the
pattern did not carry.**

## R516 — The hand-made mark, unforgeable by absence

**`scripts/lib/assembly-mark.ts`.** Three states — `GENERATED_FROM_ROWS`, `ASSEMBLED_BY_HAND`,
`GENERATED_THEN_EDITED` — with a `readAs` line that prints **where she reads it**, not only in a stamp.

**Her reason: a generated artefact's claims about the store CAN BE WRONG AND CAN BE CHECKED, because
there is a query behind them to re-run. A hand-assembled one's cannot be checked at all.**
`narrator-redraft-proposal-0413f8ee` claimed a key that is a distractor, **and nothing could
re-derive that claim because no query produced it.**

**Meeting a claim about a key in a hand-assembled document should tell her she is reading somebody's
ACCOUNT rather than the store.** The field is a warning at the moment of reading, not provenance for
the record.

**UNFORGEABLE BY ABSENCE: no field means HAND-ASSEMBLED.** The default is the unsafe reading, because
the safe one would let an unmarked hand-written file pass as generated — **and a hand-written document
is precisely the one nobody remembers to mark.** An unknown value falls to HAND as well; **only an
explicit generated declaration reads as generated.**

`GENERATED_THEN_EDITED` reads as an account too, because **the edit is the unverifiable part and it is
not separable from the rest.** 5 tests.

## R517 — Do not narrow the data before the operation that needs it

**Her rule, REPLACING *"a match carries its kind"* — which was one instance stated as the rule.**

> **Carry everything to the point of decision and discard after.**

**The operational half is her reason: the discard always happens before anybody knows what the
decision will need, and the information is never expensive to keep and always expensive to recover.**

**The four instances:**

| instance | narrowed too early | cost |
|---|---|---|
| **direction** never asked | inbound/outbound dropped at match time | two outbound artefacts counted as stale inbound snapshots |
| **footnotes** counted as readers | import-vs-mention dropped at match time | seven still-read files that were one |
| **serialisation** not carried | JSON-vs-markdown dropped before matching | 944 artefacts, zero matches, a wrong pattern indistinguishable from a clean store |
| **formatting** not tolerated | `options\n.map` unmatched | the top two of a fix order misreported as non-compliant |

**Every one discarded something free and recovered it at the cost of a wrong number already
reported.**

## R518 — `export-cowork-workorder` is UNTESTED, not compliant

**Never staged. Zero uses and zero faults look identical.**

**The same word as `en-vocab-not-this-word` (R476): a STATE, not a stage. It did not pass — it was
never asked.**

**And it is last in the fix order for the right reason**: not because it is least bad, but because
**there is no occasion behind it.** An artefact that has never carried a verdict cannot have carried
one badly, and fixing it first would be work ordered by severity in a list ordered by use.

## R519 — Why the guard has caught two where no pattern has caught its own

**A wrong pattern's output over a clean population is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a right pattern's.** Zero
key-claims because the regex was wrong, and zero key-claims because nobody quotes keys, **produce the
identical result.** Nothing in the output could ever have shown it.

**`requirePopulation` does not ask WHAT WAS FOUND. It asks WHETHER ANYTHING COULD HAVE BEEN.** That is
a question about the query rather than the result, and it is the only question whose answer differs
between the two cases.

**Both catches this session were scope queries, not results**: `stem.headword` where the store has
`stem.words[0]`, and a quote where JSON has a backslash. **Neither would have been found by reading
the output, however carefully** — and the three uncaught pattern faults above all produced NON-zero
output, which is exactly the case the guard cannot reach.

**So the guard covers the empty case completely and the wrong-but-nonempty case not at all**, and
R517 is what covers the second.

## R520 — Scan-output rows join the claim ledger

**Her ruling, 2026-08-21.** **A scan's classification is a CLAIM, the object is the ARTEFACT, and the
comparison is OPENING IT.** Same kind as every row already in the ledger.

**The only reason they were not there is that a table does not read like a claim.** *"key-only"* in a
column reads as a measurement; written out it is *"this artefact shows an option without its
siblings"* — **a sentence about a file, checkable only by opening the file**, which is the ledger's
definition exactly.

**And the session proves the population is live**: `export-review-pack` was classified key-only and
renders every option with its key. **Three such misclassifications in two turns, each reported as a
measurement, each settled by opening the file.**

## R521 — The ledger's proportionate form: read what you will act on

**Recorded with the scan rows because the population is now large and the useful part is not.**

**Read the rows you will act on — always a handful, always the ones that matter — and let the rest sit
COUNTED AND UNREAD.**

**The ledger is not a work queue and completing it was never the goal.** 1,092 claims plus scan
outputs is a population to draw from, and **its value is that a row can be found when it matters, not
that every row is read.** An unread row is not a debt; it is a claim nobody has needed to check.

**This is what stops the ledger becoming the backlog it was built to measure** — the failure it would
otherwise repeat is the conditional-flag population, where nine rows in an obligation field read as
nine obligations and were two.

## R522 — The guard's bound is PERMANENT, not current

**Both catches empty. All three uncaught faults non-empty. That ratio is a property, not a state.**

**A wrong pattern that FINDS SOMETHING looks exactly like a right pattern that finds something.** No
count separates them — both produce a plausible number. No emptiness test reaches them — neither is
empty. **And a second pattern is only a second belief about the same property**, which is why writing
one is not a check.

**`requirePopulation` covers the empty case COMPLETELY and the wrong-but-nonempty case NOT AT ALL**,
and no extension of it can change that: it asks whether anything could have been found, and something
was.

**So the second case has no instrument and is not going to get one.** R517 — carry everything to the
point of decision — is not a mitigation of this bound but the only thing that operates on the other
side of it: **it prevents the narrowing rather than detecting its consequence.**

## R523 — Her prediction: source varies in formatting by nature, and eight scans assume it does not

**Not a new rule — a prediction about R517, naming where it fires next.**

**A pattern over SOURCE that assumes a line shape is assuming the least stable property source has.**
Formatting is the one thing a linter, a refactor or a hand edit changes freely and silently.

**Checked, as she asked. EIGHT scans read source with line-shape-assuming patterns — 44 patterns
between them:**

| risky | scan |
|---:|---|
| 11 | `check-walkscript-reach` |

## R536 — Internal consistency is evidence that nothing has changed, not that anything is right

**The finding the failed amendment demonstrates, which had no name.**

**A consistency check compares a row against itself.** `en-unstressed-suffix-vowel` was *internally
consistent* — narrow description, matching hint — **and it was consistent BECAUSE the widening had
failed.** The mismatch was between her intent and the row, **and no check compares those**.

**So a row can be tidy for the worst reason: nothing reached it.** An entry whose amendment landed and
whose hint was then left behind looks *inconsistent* and gets found; an entry whose amendment never
landed looks *clean*.

**AND THE TIDIER IT LOOKS, THE LESS ANYTHING WILL ASK.** Consistency is the property most likely to be
read as health and least likely to prompt a lookup — which is why the 44 flagged by
`check:widened-without-hint` are a better population than the entries it passed.

**Her rule: when she checks an artefact for staleness she checks it against THE STORE, because her
record is a list of her own decisions and silent about everybody else's.**

**A reviewer's own record is the one artefact guaranteed to omit every change she did not make** — and
it is also the one she will reach for first, because it is hers and it is complete about the thing she
was thinking of.

## R543 — Every unverified population is an UPPER BOUND, not an estimate

**Her finding, and it is a direction rather than modesty about counting.**

**The inflation that puts errors at the head of an ordering also puts them in the sum.**

| population | as first reported | after verification |
|---|---:|---:|
| non-compliant artefacts | 22 | 12 → **10 → 6** |
| still-read snapshots | 7 | 3 → **1** |
| `en-plausible-not-stated` carriers | 209 | **27** |
| `en-attribute-transfer` carriers | 97 | **43** |
| scans with risky patterns | 8 | **5** |
| risky patterns | 44 | **14** |
| vowel-entry carriers | 8 | **3** |

**Every one shrank. None has ever grown.**

**The mechanism is that a pattern which over-matches produces both the wrong head and the wrong
total**, and the head gets corrected because somebody acts on it while the total is only ever quoted.
**So a verified count is a floor and an unverified one is a ceiling**, and the gap between them is
whatever the pattern could not distinguish.

## R544 — The two repairs the element inverts: one label is the content, one should not exist

**Her ruling, applied 2026-08-21. Opposite acts on one fault, and only the element separates them.**

**THE LANTERN — the label was the content, and it was SUPPRESSING the authored voice line.**
`role="img"` plus `aria-label` makes a reader announce the **label** and **ignore the children
entirely**. So a child heard *"Streak lantern: alive"* and **never heard *"Lantern's still lit."*** —
the authored sentence sitting immediately beside it, written for exactly this moment.

**That is worse than the machine syntax I reported.** The fault was not a poor label; it was a label
**replacing** a good sentence. The emoji stays `aria-hidden`, the `role="img"` and the label are gone,
**and the voice line now reaches the ear exactly as it reaches the eye.**

**THE MASCOT — the fault is not that the sentence is poor, it is that the sentence exists.** It is
decoration. With `role="img"` and a label it announced an animation tag — *"Your detective friend is
pointing"* — **every time the pose changed**, on a 20-second idle timer, **interrupting whatever a
child was listening to.** It carries no information she needs and no act she can take. **`aria-hidden`
is the repair: decoration announces nothing.**

**Two labels, one fault, opposite repairs — and the string alone chooses neither.**

**Staged: `TWO-SCREEN-READER-TRANSCRIPTS.md`, `f318b31ebc3af9f5…`. Not an audit, and it must not

sentence has to.* **In the ear there is no layout** — it follows *"and her pencil case."* as though it

**The walk panel.** Each tap adds a paragraph **above** the button, and **there is no live region** —
so a child hears nothing change until she moves focus back up. The button's label changing from *Next
bit* to *Close* is the only signal the walk has ended.

**No verdict from here on whether this is ten strings or a fourth review scope. She cannot tell that
from where she is, and neither can anyone else** — which is why the two transcripts are the whole

## R546 — Line 3 does not contain the sentence, and the preview is the repair

**Her question, answered in one line: NO.** Transcript line 3 is *"The sentence, in four parts. Choose
the part with the mistake."* — **a description of the sentence, not the sentence.**

**So my commentary was wrong.** I wrote that the sentence is *"announced twice: once as the group's
name, then segment by segment"*. **It is announced once**, as four button labels. **With the preview
`aria-hidden`, a child never hears the sentence as continuous prose at any width.**

**And the preview's own comment gave the false reason**: *"a screen reader already receives the
sentence once, through the group below."* **It does not.** The group's name describes the sentence; the
buttons carry its pieces.

**HER RULING: THE PREVIEW IS NOT DECORATION, IT IS THE REPAIR.** It exists because below 600px the
segments cannot read inline — **the same deficit exists in the ear at every width**, and the element
that fixes it was hidden from the only reader who always has it. `aria-hidden` removed.

## R547 — Focus moves to the sentence, because the sentence is the content

**Applied.** Each tap added a paragraph above the button and announced nothing; a child heard no change
until she moved focus back up herself.

**Not a live region.** The newest sentence takes focus with `tabIndex={-1}` — programmatic focus
without entering the tab order, so a child tabbing through still meets only the button.

**Her reason is the shape: the sentence is the CONTENT and the button is the MECHANISM.** Focus goes to
the content, **and then the ending is a PLACE she arrives at rather than a label changing under her
focus.** A live region would have announced the new text while leaving her standing on a button whose
name had silently changed.
