***Walk this one with me* is a first person in an accessible name.** She refused the persona in the
Daily Loop copy and ruled it a product decision to be taken deliberately rather than inside a mode fix.

**It was ruled nowhere.** It appears in no return except the one flagging it, in no register entry, and
**it entered in commit `7dffe51` — mine — when I built the panel.** I introduced a refused persona into
the first thing a child using a screen reader hears from that surface.

**REMOVED, NOT REWORDED.** The only other candidate string, `'Walk through it with me'`, **carries the
same first person**, so there is no approved non-persona name to fall back to — **and authoring one
here would be the same act again.** The `role="group"` and its name are gone; the paragraphs read as
paragraphs, and a name can be added when one is authored.

## R549 — Where a visual distinction carries meaning, the same meaning is carried in structure or words

**Her general form, recorded above the four repairs.** **Not the same appearance — the same MEANING.**

The errorspot verdict is the case: a pill on its own line, and the code says *"the layout says
'different kind of thing' so no sentence has to."* **The structure already carries it** — the verdict
sits outside the `role="group"`, so a boundary is announced. **Checked rather than changed.** The
design was right and only its comment assumed a modality.

**The rule refuses two wrong repairs.** Reproducing the appearance in words — *"and separately, a fifth
option"* — restates the layout rather than its meaning. And lengthening the button's label restates
what the stem already said. **Structure carries a boundary better than any sentence, and it was already
there.**

## R550 — Not every hidden element needs its label written as content

**What the lantern taught, and it is the opposite of the mascot's repair.**

**Some need the label REMOVED so the content can speak.** `role="img"` suppressed *"Lantern's still
lit."* — a sentence already written, already approved, sitting immediately beside it. **The repair was
deletion, and the content was never missing.**

**The mascot needed the same deletion for the opposite reason**: there was no content, and the label
was manufacturing some.

**So `aria-hidden` and a removed label look identical in the diff and mean opposite things.** One says
*this element has nothing to say*; the other says *this element's children are already saying it.*
**A rule of the form "hidden elements need labels" produces the first repair correctly and the second
one backwards.**

## R551 — Code comments join the claim ledger

**Her ruling.** **The object is the ANNOUNCEMENT ORDER. The comparison is a TRANSCRIPT. The transcript
took one document to produce.**

Two comments this week asserted a property of a surface and were wrong about it:

- the errorspot preview: *"a screen reader already receives the sentence once, through the group
  below"* — **it does not**, the group's name describes the sentence rather than carrying it;
- the errorspot verdict: *"the layout says 'different kind of thing' so no sentence has to"* —
  **correct on screen, and the structure happened to carry it in the ear too, which the comment did
  not claim and did not check.**

**BOTH WROTE THEIR ASSUMPTION DOWN AT THE MOMENT IT WAS MADE, WHICH IS MORE HONEST THAN MOST DESIGN
REASONING EVER GETS.** The fault is not that somebody assumed. **It is that nothing read the
assumptions back against the surface** — and a comment asserting a fact about what a child perceives
is a claim about a text with code as the text, which is the ledger's shape exactly.

**Cheap, because the comparison already exists**: one transcript settled both.

## R552 — Identical acts with opposite reasons: the reason goes where the act is

**Her rule.** **The two deletions are byte-identical.** The lantern's label was **suppressing content
that existed**; the mascot's was **manufacturing content that did not.**

**A diff cannot carry that, and a rule reasoning from the ACT gets one right and the other backwards.**
*"Hidden elements need labels"* repairs the mascot correctly and re-breaks the lantern.

**So the reason goes where the act is** — in the code, beside the deletion, not only in a register
entry a future reader may not reach.

**Third instance of the shape**: the **PU-08 library ruling** (a decision not to serve, recorded so it
could not read as an omission — R399) and the **hold lifted deliberately rather than by inheritance**
(R455). **All three are acts whose meaning is invisible in their result.**

## R553 — Check rather than follow: twice this week a sound thing was nearly moved

**Her note.** She ruled a change to something **already correct** — the errorspot verdict's group
boundary — and **had the ruling been implemented rather than checked, something sound would have been
moved for a reason that did not apply to it.**

**Twice this week.** The other was `export-review-pack`, first in a fix order she was asked to act on
and **already compliant**; three of that order's heads were.

**The general form: a ruling names a property, and the check asks whether THIS instance already has
it.** Implementing directly assumes the instance is an example of the fault, **which is exactly what a
misclassification supplies** — and five of those this fortnight all pointed at things that turned out
correct.

## R554 — The persona decision is David's, and declining it into silence is not deciding it

**Recorded because it has now been refused once and arrived anyway twice.**

She refused first person in the **Daily Loop copy** and ruled it a product decision to be taken
deliberately rather than inside a mode fix. **It then entered as `Walk this one with me`** — a group
label, **the first thing a child using a screen reader hears from that surface.** Removed twice, and
**the only other candidate string, `Walk through it with me`, carries the same first person.**

**The walk panel now reads `How this one works out`**, hers, from the Daily Loop line already approved
— **and she declined to author a replacement into the gap on the grounds that it would be the same act
one turn later with her name on it.**

**HER POINT: the third time it arrives it will be somewhere neither of them is looking**, and the
pattern is that **it arrives in the quietest available place rather than in copy anyone reviews.**

**The question, and it is David's: does anything in this product speak to a child in the first
person?** Nothing does **right now, by accident rather than by ruling.**

**Neither answer is the safe one.** No wants writing down, so an authoring instinct meets a rule
instead of a gap. Yes wants a scope — **which surfaces, in what voice, and who authors it** — because
the instinct producing *walk this one with me* and *I'll show you how I worked this out* is trying to
make a product that talks to a nine-year-old sound like a person, **and that is not a bad instinct to
have arrive unruled twice.**

## R555 — The first-person scanner, built to the scope rather than to the pronoun

**David's ruling, 2026-08-21.** `pnpm check:first-person`. **Refused** in accessible names, group
labels, button labels and status text. **Permitted** in mode and hint copy **only where a reviewer's
authority is on the string.** **A first-person string with no reviewer citation is refused wherever it
sits.**

**Current state: 0 refused, 0 permitted.** Nothing in the product speaks in the first person, and now
by ruling rather than by accident.

**THE CONSEQUENCE FOR SOURCE IS TOTAL AND DELIBERATE.** No string in a `.tsx` file can carry a
reviewer citation, because **there is no field to carry one** — so every first-person string in source
is refused by the provenance rule even where position would permit it. **That is the scope working:
both arrivals were in source, both unreviewable, both in the quietest place available.**

**TWO EXCLUSIONS, BOTH FOUND BY RUNNING IT, AND BOTH ARE R320 AND R349 REACHING A NEW SCANNER.**

**A quotation is not the product speaking.** *"Go and fetch my fishing-rod"* is Bevis; *"what do I see
at the bottom but a heap of rolls"* is Dickens. Quoted spans are stripped before matching.

**The analytic `we` is a comprehension convention, not a persona.** *"we are never told what it is"*
means *the text does not say*. **Reported separately, never refused** — and **the scope does not
distinguish them in writing, which is a gap for the ruling rather than for the check.**

**AND `walkScript` IS OUT OF SCOPE, WHICH THE CHECK SAYS ON ITS FACE.** 43 walk scripts carry a
first-person or analytic token and **a pronoun test cannot separate the product's voice from what it
reports**: `I` is **a letter** in every VR series script (*"so I moves one on to J"*), and reported
speech arrives unquoted (*"Line 22 says and I have"*). **Whose voice a sentence is in is a reading, not
a match** — the pointing band and the paraphrase band in a third place.

## R556 — Seventy child-facing strings sit in source, outside copy review

**The surfaces the instinct goes to when reviewed copy is closed to it. 72 files scanned.**

| strings | surface |
|---:|---|
| **32** | accessible names (`aria-label`, `alt`, `title`) |
| **19** | headings |
| **16** | plain paragraph literals |
| 2 | button labels |
| 1 | status / live region |
| 0 | placeholders |

**70 distinct strings, none of which has a reviewer, a provenance field, or an amendment path.** A
return cannot amend any of them: **there is no id to name and no row to write.**

**IS THE LIST COMPLETE? NO, AND THE HONEST ANSWER IS THAT IT CANNOT BE MADE COMPLETE BY THIS METHOD.**
It finds string literals in six syntactic positions. **It cannot see** a string built by
concatenation, one held in a constant and rendered elsewhere, one reaching the surface through a
helper, or any string in a file outside the four crew directories.

**So 70 is a floor** (R543: every unverified population is an upper bound — **and this one is the
opposite, because the method under-matches rather than over-matching**). The two arrivals that
prompted the ruling were both **accessible names**, which is the largest row.

**What the scope buys is not coverage — it is that the largest and quietest surface now has a rule on
it.** The 19 headings and 16 paragraphs remain unreviewed, and naming them is the finding rather than
the repair.

## R557 — The permission withdrawn: first person refused everywhere, in two kinds

**David, 2026-08-21. The scope becomes a specification.** First person is refused **everywhere today**,
and `check:first-person` distinguishes the two refusals rather than flattening them:

**PERMANENT** — accessible names, group labels, button labels, status text. **A persona has no place
in a control's name whatever is decided about voice.**

**PENDING** — mode and hint copy, refused **until a body decision exists**, and **the refusal says so
on its face**: *"PENDING, not banned… a hold on an open question."*

**A REFUSAL THAT HIDES ITS OWN REASON IS HOW A PENDING DECISION BECOMES A PERMANENT ONE NOBODY EVER
MADE.** The scanner's message is the only place a future author meets this, and *"refused"* alone
would retire the question exactly as a scan name retires a scope (R541).

**The Daily Loop line stays third person as she wrote it**, and `How this one works out` stands.

## R558 — The fourth mechanism is plumbing, and the plumbing is done

**Where the read-gate stands: `ACTIVE-AND-SERVING`.** Seven LIVE items serve their own hint — the nine
punctuation items minus PU-08 (ruled to the library) and PU-03 (held, then approved).

| | |
|---|---:|
| items carrying a `hintCore` | 373 |
| of those LIVE | 43 |
| read by a named reviewer | 14 (7 LIVE) |
| **LIVE, carrying a hint, still unread** | **36** |

**THE GATE IS NOT THE OBSTACLE. IT ALREADY FLIPPED**, the moment she ruled nine strings.

**Serving the rest costs nothing to build.** Each of the 36 becomes served **by being read** — no
deploy, no schema, no decision beyond the hint. **And there is no fallback case anywhere**: all 43
route to a library hint on every wrong option, so every read is a straight replacement of a shared
hint by a specific one. **At her rate — nine in one pass — the 36 is four passes.**

**AND THIS IS THE GAP THE PRONOUN WAS BEING ASKED TO FILL.** A library hint is written to be true of
every carrier of a tag, so on any particular item it is **general by construction**. The item's own
hint is the specific thing and **it sat authored and unread**: `PU-02` served the general sentence
while its own reached nobody until four days ago.

**A voice is not what makes a hint specific. A hint written for the item is.**

## R559 — A forbidden thing relocates to the channel where nobody looks

**Her generalisation, and it reaches much further than persona.**

**Copy flows to the least-reviewed channel the way water finds low ground, and forbidding it in the
reviewed channels only steepens the slope.**

**So a rule that forbids without providing a permitted route pushes the thing into the unwatched
channel** — and the repair is **a route plus a gate**, never a prohibition alone.

**The ten aria-labels are that mechanism's output, by drift rather than intent.** Nobody decided to put
product voice in accessible names. **The reviewed channels were closed and that one was open**, and it
had no reviewer, no provenance field and no amendment path — which is what made it the low ground.

**The pattern is already in this register three times over and was never named**: the conditional-flag
obligations that lived in a recommendation sentence because no field existed for them (R347); the
hand-assembled proposals whose claims about rows nothing could re-derive (R516); the seventy source
strings outside copy review (R556). **Each is content arriving in the only channel that would take it.**

**And the corollary is the operational half: when a rule is written, the question is not only what it
forbids but WHERE THE THING IT FORBIDS WILL GO INSTEAD.** R557's pending refusal is written to that —
it names the open decision rather than closing the channel silently, so the next author meets a
question rather than a wall.

## R560 — A replacement needs the thing it replaces: sixth home for the rule

**Her standing ruling, 2026-08-22.** The thirty-six re-presented as
`unread-item-hints-for-annie-6c5150db96cb3f0b.json`, `4c26be993aaa889d…` — **each row carrying all
four required things**: the item and its stem, its options **with the key marked**, its own
`hintCore`, and **the library hint(s) it would replace**, per option.

**A hint that is worse than the general one it replaces is a REGRESSION DRESSED AS SPECIFICITY**, and
that is invisible without both strings.

**Sixth home for one rule.** An option needs its key and siblings; a card needs every item it serves;
a label needs its element; a template needs its values; a claim needs its text; **a replacement needs
the thing it replaces.** **Nothing is judged out of the set it belongs to, and the sender always holds
the set** — which is the half that makes it the sender's obligation rather than the reader's request.

## R561 — Twelve staged since her manifest, and the manifest has an age too

**Nothing has crossed since her held manifest was taken at 21:15 on 21 August.** Twelve artefacts
staged after it — the transcripts, the ten heard strings, the templates, the vowel split, the
narrator carriers, the read-gate report, and the thirty-six.

**AND THE DIFF CANNOT TELL *NOT CROSSED* FROM *CROSSED AFTER THE MANIFEST WAS TAKEN*.** Her manifest
is a snapshot with a timestamp, so **everything staged after it reads as absent whether or not it
arrived.**

**That is her taken-against ruling arriving on the manifest itself** — an artefact assembled from more
than one moment carries the age of its oldest part, and the oldest part of this comparison is the
manifest. **A manifest needs its own taken-against line as much as a transcript does.**

## R562 — The transcript re-rendered, and my first one omitted a boundary that was there

**`PU-02-TRANSCRIPT-RERENDERED.md`, `81f3edde33a2589c…`, with a taken-against block: build `852ed8f`,
gate `ACTIVE-AND-SERVING`, row digest `58258ff99d867781…`.**

**Three lines changed.** The preview is no longer hidden, so **line 3 is the sentence as continuous
prose** — heard before it is heard as four buttons. **Line 11 is her hint**, not the library's.

**And line 9 — *"Group end"* — was always in the DOM and my first transcript omitted it**, which made
the verdict read as a fifth part of the sentence. **The structure was right and the transcript was
wrong**, and I reported the structure as the fault.

**From now every transcript carries the taken-against block**: build, gate state, and the digest of the
row it announced. **Mine was a rendering of the product as it stood before the gate flipped**, and
nothing on its face said so.

## R563 — When a channel is created, its reviewer is created with it

**Her forward prediction, built into the act.** `pnpm check:channel-has-reviewer`. **A channel is any
file putting a literal sentence in front of a child**; its reviewer is one line at the top:
`// COPY-REVIEW: <who rules the strings here, and where that is recorded>`.

**The walk panel is the evidence**: built this fortnight, and a refused persona was in its group label
within days — **not because anyone decided to put it there, but because it was new, and new means
unwatched.**

**Current state: 28 channels, 0 with a declared reviewer.** Reports rather than fails — assigning one
to every existing channel is a governance act, not a commit.

**THE RULE BITES ON A NEW CHANNEL.** One line at the moment of building, **which is the only moment it
is cheap** — and it gets ahead of R559's mechanism rather than chasing it, because the low ground is
created before anything flows into it.

## R564 — I renamed the field, so a lookup by its own name returned nothing on 36 of 36

**Her report: `hintCore` is null on thirty-six of thirty-six, checked row by row.** **It is not null —
I renamed it.** The rows carried `itsOwnHint`, so `row.hintCore` was `undefined` on every one, and the
values were present the whole time: *"The very first line names the morning. Start there."*

**A FIELD RENAMED IN AN ARTEFACT IS A FIELD ABSENT TO ANYONE WHO KNOWS IT.** I renamed it for
readability, in a delivery to the person whose every ruling uses the original name. **Restored**, and
re-staged as `unread-item-hints-for-annie-bf31491e2bb99b50.json`, `f71b1c98e781bc9a…` — **0 nulls
across 36.**

**AND THE FIGURES RECONCILE, WHICH SETTLES WHAT KIND OF ACT THIS IS.** 1033 items, 341 LIVE. **373
carry a hintCore, 43 of those LIVE, 14 read (7 LIVE) — and 43 − 7 = 36.**

**So the 36 are LIVE items that ALREADY CARRY an authored hint awaiting a read. They are a READ, not
an authoring job**, and her nine-at-a-time rate applies at reading speed. **The LIVE items with no item
hint are a different population of 298**, not here, and not what she was sent.

## R565 — The group label asserted a mistake exists, on an item where there is not one

**Her fifth-return ruling removed that assertion from all eighteen stems.** The group label survived
it: *"The sentence, in four parts. **Choose the part with the mistake.**"*

**`ENG-003-A-PU-09`'s key is `No mistake`.** The label told a child to choose the part with the mistake
on an item whose answer is that there is not one — **while the stem beside it reads *"One part MAY have
a punctuation mistake… If every part is right, choose No mistake."***

**THE STEMS WERE CORRECTED IN THE REVIEWED CHANNEL AND THE COPY SURVIVED IN THE UNREVIEWED ONE** — not
because anybody moved it, but because **nothing looked there when the eighteen were fixed.** R559's
mechanism arriving on schedule, on the surface where it was predicted.

**Her amendment loses the instruction rather than gaining a hedge**: `"The sentence, in four parts."`
The stem already instructs; the label describes the container — the same shape as `How this one works
out`.

**THE AUDIT SHE ASKED FOR: 62 accessible names, group labels and status strings screened across every
child surface. ZERO others assert a fault exists.** The full set is delivered for her reading, because
a match tests one ruling and she has made many.

## R566 — The doubling is deliberate, recorded before somebody tidies it

**Reading is parallel and listening is serial.** A child hears the sentence whole (the preview), then
hears it again in four parts (the buttons) — **twenty-two words twice, at speaking speed.**

**That is the right cost, because the alternative is never hearing it whole.** A sighted child takes
the sentence in at a glance and the segments are simply how she chooses; a listening child has no
glance, and without the preview the sentence exists for her only as four disconnected button labels.

**RECORDED BEFORE SOMEBODY TIDIES IT, because removing it for tidiness and removing it for her look
identical in a diff.** Third instance of that shape — after the two byte-identical `aria-hidden`
deletions (R552) and the PU-08 library ruling (R399).

## R567 — English hints instructing a visual act: 8 library, 22 item

**English only.** `ENGLISH-HINTS-INSTRUCTING-A-VISUAL-ACT.md`, `c30350186144204e…`. **8 of 70 English
library hints** and **22 English item hints** carry a word instructing a visual act.

**The matched word is marked on every row because the judgement is hers**: *see* in *see the line* is a
reading act and *see* in *see the shape* is not, **and a match cannot tell them apart.**

**AND NVR IS RAISED OUT LOUD RATHER THAN DISCOVERED, which is what she asked for.** It is not in the
file. **Every NVR hint instructs a visual act by construction** — the district is about shapes — so the
question is not a defect list but **whether that district is servable to her at all.** Asking it is the
deliverable; answering it is not mine.

## R568 — Print the keys present before reading the values (Annie's rule)

**A null from a renamed field and a null from an empty field are the same value.**

She read all thirty-six rows of `unread-item-hints-for-annie` — not the head, every row — found
`hintCore` null on each, and concluded the population was thirty-six items with **no** hint. The
reading was correct and the conclusion followed from it. The field was there, under `itsOwnHint`,
in the same object, one line away, because I had renamed it for readability in a delivery to the
person whose every ruling uses the original name (R564).

**THE CARE WAS REAL AND IT WAS SPENT ON THE WRONG AXIS.** Checking every row tests whether the value
is missing *somewhere*. **It cannot test whether the NAME is right, because a rename is uniform** —
the answer is identical on every row, so no amount of row-wise thoroughness separates it from an
empty field. **The keys present are a different measurement, and it is one line.**

`readFieldsByName()` in `scripts/lib/field-read.ts` prints the union of keys actually present with
their row counts, then reports each requested name as present-and-non-empty, present-and-empty, or
**NOT A KEY ON ANY ROW — which THROWS.** A name on zero rows is not an empty population, and
`requirePopulation` cannot see it: that guard counts rows and cannot tell that they are the wrong
rows.

**IT PAID ON ITS FIRST RUN.** One line —
`walkScript(340) walkScriptBatch(297) hintCore(43) hintAuthority(8) hintAuthoredBy(7)` — carries the
whole 43 − 7 = 36 arithmetic that took a return, a correction and a reconciliation to establish, and
shows an asymmetry nobody had asked about: **8 items carry `hintAuthority` and 7 carry
`hintAuthoredBy`**, and `chooseHint` requires both.

**THE POPULATION: 34 delivery scripts read a JSON column field by name; 1 carries the guard.**
`pnpm check:field-reads` derives that population (R57) and **ratchets on a FLOOR rather than failing
thirty-four scripts on its first run** — a check that is red on the day it lands gets muted inside a
week, which this board has named three times. The floor names no script, so it cannot bless one.

## R569 — A match carries what it matched on, and that is provenance in its smallest useful form

**What made `ENGLISH-HINTS-INSTRUCTING-A-VISUAL-ACT.md` readable was one column: the matched word,
marked on every row.**

Without it she would have had to reconstruct, for each of thirty rows, why that row was in the file —
and the reconstruction is the expensive half, because *see* in *see the line* is a reading act and
*see* in *see the shape* is not. **With it, half the file resolved to no in seconds.**

This is the same rule as R472's option sets, R555's element-and-what-it-does, and R560's four fields,
**reduced to its smallest instance: a match that carries its own evidence.** The general form is
**A RESULT TRAVELS WITH THE THING THAT PRODUCED IT** — a matched word, a quoted span, a computed
value's inputs. A row that says only *this matched* asks the reader to re-run the matcher by hand,
which is the R25 fault (an account instead of the value) arriving inside a delivery that is otherwise
exemplary.

## R570 — The amendment reader knew one of her four shapes, and both sides shared the edit that hid it

**`en-repetition-purpose` and `en-motive-invention` held the wordings she REPLACED**, in returns
reported applied. Neither had landed, and `check:amendments-landed` reported both returns FULLY
LANDED — because it never read the amendments at all.

**FOUR SHAPES, ONE READ.**

- `BLOCK` — the indented `AMENDMENTS` block, `target:` / `replaced:` / `authored:`, **no bold**.
  **She has used it for twenty-eight returns.** Both existing shapes require `**`, so every one was
  invisible. The fifty-first return's own block declares `count: 13`; the reader found **nought**.
- `LABELLED` with a **line wrap**. Her returns hard-wrap near ninety columns, so a long authored
  wording closes its `**` on the next line, and `.` cannot cross a newline. The seventeenth return
  carries three; this found one and called the return fully landed.
- `HEADED_LABELLED` — the target sitting in the bolded heading one line above. Those amendments were
  read but reported UNPLACEABLE, which is strictly weaker than absent and reads as an unfixable limit
  rather than an unread line.

**AND `apply-all-unlanded.ts` KEPT ITS OWN REGEX — R429 recurring inside the ruling that named it.**
That entry created the shared reader *because two parsers over one format disagree eventually*, and
the apply script never imported it. **The second parser survived the ruling about second parsers.**

**THE NORMALISER WAS EDITING HER TEXT, AND BOTH SIDES AGREED BECAUSE THEY SHARED THE MUTILATION.**
`tidy()` unwrapped lines *and stripped a trailing full stop*. The second half is not normalisation —
it is a silent edit to an authored value, and `checkChildFacingText` requires a child-facing sentence
to end on a full stop. So eleven rows whose stored text was **already correct** read as different and
were queued to be rewritten **without their full stop**, including `en-plausible-not-stated` — 193
carriers, 11 LIVE, the most-carried hint in the product. The check could not see it because its own
comparison stripped the stop too. **NORMALISE WHERE YOU COMPARE; NEVER WHERE YOU READ.**

**THREE CLASSES, NOT ONE.** *Not in the store* was reported as ABSENT and is three different facts:
**SUPERSEDED** (a later amendment to the same row did land — she changed her mind, and rewriting the
earlier wording would run the return leg backwards), **UNPLACEABLE** (read from a shape carrying no
target), **ABSENT** (a named row that does not hold her ruling). Reporting the first as absent
manufactures work and would have undone three of her decisions.

**AND THE PARENTHETICAL NAMES THE FIELD.** `en-vocab-neighbouring-sense (description, not hint)` — the
first `resolveTarget` stripped the bracket to get a clean id, aiming an adult-facing description at
`childHint`. It aborted on the gate, which is luck: **had it read like a hint it would have been
written where a child sees it.** Then the guard against it, `/hint/i.test('description, not hint')`,
returned **true** — matching the field she was *excluding*. Her form is `<field>, not <other field>`;
the field is the part before the comma.

**THE GUARD IS HER OWN COUNT.** `declaredCounts()` reads `count: N` from her block and fails when the
reader extracts fewer. `describeShapes()` printed the shapes truthfully on every run — R60's
discipline, working exactly as designed — **and it could not help, because nothing compared the
declared shapes to the shapes the source actually used.** A count comes from the other side of that
gap.

**OUTCOME: 33 → 71 wordings read; 15 genuinely-absent library hints written and confirmed by reading
each row back; not-in-the-store 25 → 10.** Residual: **4 word-card definitions** (`stoic` ×2, `shiny`,
`luminous`) and **1 description field**, all in tables `apply-all-unlanded` does not own — reported,
not written, because a writer that reaches past its own table is the fault this register opened with.

## R571 — Candidate coaching is measurable by two routes, and the third band is not

**Her question: can a check find a hint that gives its own key away — and if it can only find
containment, say that, because the pointing band has been ruled unreachable before.**

**Both routes reach, and NEITHER ALONE would have found both known cases.**

- **CONTAINMENT** — the hint reuses the key's own content words. `WIW-05`: *"…So does the climb."*
  against key *"To show the climb went on and on and was hard work."* Shared: `climb`. Score 0.20.
- **ANCHORED POINTING** — the hint quotes a phrase; the phrase locates a sentence in the passage;
  **the key's content is in that sentence.** `WIW-12`: the hint quotes *'never in his life'*, which
  lands on *"Never in his life had he seen a river before…"*, and the key is *"A river."*

**`WIW-12` SHARES NOT ONE CONTENT WORD WITH ITS KEY — containment scores it 0.00.** It is invisible
to the obvious check and it is the *clearer* of the two faults. A single-route detector would have
found one of two and looked like it worked, which is the shape this register keeps meeting.

**WHAT IS NOT REACHABLE, AND IT IS NOT CLAIMED: pointing by DESCRIBING rather than quoting.**
*"Read the sentence that comes just before he throws the brush down"* carries no locatable anchor;
matching a description to a moment is a reading, not a lookup. **13 of 36 hints are in that band and
the count is printed on every run**, so an empty pointing result can never read as a clean bank.
**`WIW-10` — one of the three she amended — is in that band.** The check did not surface it and says
so.

**5 candidates from 36: 1 by pointing, 4 by containment.** Two are her confirmed faults; **three sit
in batches she has not read, so the precision of this check is UNMEASURED, not measured-good.**
Every row is a candidate marked with what it matched on (R569) — the verdict is hers (R94).

**And the same run answered a question nobody asked**: scanning the 36 for her `WIW-03` shouted-capital
fault found **2 of 36** — `WIW-03`, which she ruled, and **`WIW-20`, in batch 3, unread.** A ruling
applied to its population rather than its row.

## R572 — Item hints and library hints take different questions, so the artefacts differ

**She has ruled the review split by KIND, and the split is structural rather than a quality
difference between the two.**

    AN ITEM HINT    is read against its KEY      — does it give the answer away?
    A LIBRARY HINT  is read against its CARRIERS — does one wording fit them all?

**The characteristic failures follow from the definitions.** An item hint is written by somebody
looking at a single item, and **the sentence that settles that item is the sentence that contains the
answer** — so it coaches. **A library hint cannot make that mistake**, because it does not know which
item it will land on; its failure is the opposite one, generality so wide it fits everything and
helps nobody. Two of five item-hint faults so far are coaching; seven of nine library hints on those
same items are one generic *check the line numbers*. **Two characteristic failures, not a league
table.**

**WHICH MOVES THE SIX KEY-ONLY EXPORTERS OFF THIS PATH ENTIRELY.** A key without its siblings is a
defect in an ITEM-level artefact (R472), and the library-hint fit reading was being held behind them.
It does not want an option set. **It wants the items the entry lands on — and no exporter produced
those.** `export-misconception-library` delivers every entry's verbatim `childHint` plus a gate
verdict, which is the transform read, and carries no carriers. **The reading was not deferred. It had
no artefact.**

`pnpm deliver:library-carriers` is it: every English library entry with at least one carrier, each
carrying every item it lands on — the item's stem, its status, its question type, and the exact
option the entry tags. **52 entries, ordered by carrier count, because fit is hardest where reach is
widest.** `en-plausible-not-stated` reaches **193 items across 4 question types** on one sentence;
that is 193 chances for a fit to fail, and it is where *"does it fit them all"* stops being
rhetorical.

## R573 — The set is three parts, not two: the key, its siblings, and THEIR TAGS

**"Send the option set" hides the third part, and the next thing built to satisfy the phrase will
build what the phrase says.** So the parts are named on the face of the artefact.

**HER INSTANCE, AND IT IS DECISIVE.** `ENG-001-WIW-10` asks what the Mole's treatment of the rabbits
shows about him; the hint is *"Find the two words the writer uses to describe the Mole in this bit."*
**Two words, two readings, and no reason to prefer either** — until the tags are present:

        "He is frightened of the older rabbit."         en-emotion-label-approximation
        "He is so excited that he will not stop…"       KEY
        "He is a cruel animal who is always unkind."    en-extreme-option-pull   <- the one
        "He is rushing home to get his dinner."         en-motive-invention
        "He is sorry at once for knocking the rabbit…"  en-plausible-not-stated

**Option C carries the extreme where every sibling carries something milder.** The tags are not
metadata about the set; they are the half that answers her question.

`threePartSet()` in `scripts/lib/option-set.ts` is the single builder — six hand-written shapes would
be R429's two-parsers fault in a new place — and it carries **the tag's own `childHint` beside the
tag id**, because an id is a name and the wording a child receives is the value (R25).

**THE SIX, RESOLVED — AND ONLY FOUR OF THEM WERE THE THING THEY WERE FILED AS.**

- Genuinely key-only, now three-part: `export-walk-ten-for-annie`, `export-walk-vr-ten`,
  `export-eng028-walk-repairs`, `export-fifteen-headwords-for-annie`.
- **`export-vr07-vr11-new` was never key-only.** Its `opts()` already marked the key with `*` and
  appended every tag. **Sixth pattern misclassification of this kind**: the detector looked for
  `options.map` and the helper says `list.map`. The pattern carried less than the source, again.
- **`export-cowork-workorder` was aborting on `requirePopulation`, which is why it had never once
  been staged.** The guard sat on the WRONG POPULATION — it asserted that items NEED WORK, so **a
  clean bank failed the export.** 330 DRAFT English items are screened and none needs anything.
  The screened population is now the one asserted non-empty (zero screened WOULD be a broken
  pipeline); the output population is `declareMayBeEmpty` with the denominator printed beside it,
  because *"0 items need work"* and *"nothing was examined"* are the same line without it.

**And the first three-part artefact found a library fit failure on sight**: `en-attribute-transfer`'s
hint — *"Two people are being described. Check which one each detail belongs to."* — lands on an
option about painting a house, where there are no two people at all. **The item-level artefact
surfaced a library-level fault, because the tag's wording was finally beside the option it tags.**

## R574 — The locator, split out of "coaching", which is a word for an outcome

**She split the check and the split is why it is buildable.** *Coaching* names an OUTCOME — the child
is handed the answer — and **two unrelated mechanisms produce it**:

    SHAPE A  RESTATEMENT  the hint says the key again in other words.
                          WIW-05: "The words keep going and going. So does the climb."
                          key   : "To show the climb went on and on and was hard work."
    SHAPE B  THE LOCATOR  the hint quotes a phrase; the phrase locates a sentence; the key is in it.
                          WIW-12: quotes 'never in his life' -> "Never in his life had he seen a
                          river before…", and the key is "A river."

**A restatement and a pointer have nothing in common except their effect**, and one word over both is
why she would have refused the whole check. Shape B is a LOOKUP at every step and every input is
stored — passages, keys, quoted spans. **Shape A is a reading and stays reader-only.**

**THE CONTAINMENT ROUTE IS RETIRED, and why matters more than that it is gone.** It scored `WIW-05`
at 0.20 on the shared word `climb` — but `climb` is the TOPIC, not the answer, so it fired on a word
the hint could not avoid using. **It found a real fault by a mechanism that was not the fault's
mechanism** — R173's shape — and keeping it would have made the restatement band look covered. Its
other three rows were never confirmed; all sat in batches she had not read.

**THE BOUND TRAVELS AS A COUNT, NOT A CAVEAT (her instruction).** `check:hint-locator` prints, every
run: **7 hints contain a quoted string — the population, and findable. 29 point by DESCRIBING —
unfindable.** 1 candidate: `WIW-12`.

**THE 3-GRAM DRAFT IS RECORDED AS REFUSED, not merely absent.** An earlier version also tried every
3-gram of the hint against the passage — more matches, better-looking recall. **It widened the
population past the bound she set**, and the run would then have printed *"unfindable where it
describes"* while quietly searching hints that describe. **A check that breaks its own stated bound
is worse than one that misses**, because the bound is the only thing the reader is trusting. Quoted
spans only.

## R575 — A queue that can run in any order yields to a queue that cannot start

**Her scheduling, and it reverses an order I had defended.** The item-hint queue needs the KEY, which
it has, **so it runs now with nothing owed** and its passes may be taken in any order. The
library-hint queue needs the CARRIERS — **so it has not started, rather than been deferred.**

I had filed the six key-only exporters as tidiness and put them behind the remaining item-hint
passes. **They are what unblocks half the hint corpus**, and the item passes lose nothing by waiting,
because nothing about them is ordered. **The right question is not which job is more valuable but
which queue is blocked**, and only one of them was.

## R576 — `en-attribute-transfer`: the hint fits none of its LIVE carriers, and half its own definition

**The item artefact found it; only the library reading sizes it.** `threePartSet` put the tag's own
wording beside the option it tags, and the wording was *"Two people are being described. Check which
one each detail belongs to."* on an option about **painting a house**.

**One carrier is a defect. 43 carriers with no two people is a different fact**, and the difference
is the whole question she asked: **wrong for a few, or general to none?** Neither.

    43 carriers, 4 LIVE.
    17 of 43 signal two or more named people.  26 do not.
    ALL FOUR LIVE CARRIERS name at most one person.
    en-comp-vocab      0 of 8 signal two or more.
    en-comp-technique  0 of 3.
    en-comp-retrieval  9 of 23.     en-comp-inference  8 of 9.

**It fails by question type rather than at random.** On a vocabulary or technique item there are no
characters at all, so the hint does not merely fail to help — **it instructs an act the item does not
contain.** On an inference item it nearly always fits. **The wording belongs to one of the four types
it serves.**

**AND THE ENTRY CONTRADICTS ITS OWN HINT WITHOUT ANY CARRIER BEING READ.** The description: *"Assigns
one character's described attribute to another, OR THE RIGHT ATTRIBUTE AT THE WRONG VALUE."* **The
second branch needs no second person.** The hint covers one half of its own definition — a fact about
two fields sitting in one row, and nothing was comparing them.

**The signal counts NAMES, not people**, and says so on every row with the names it found: it cannot
see *the older rabbit* or *her mother*. A miss is a row to read, never a verdict.

## R577 — The general shape: a hint that ASSERTS a feature makes a testable claim

**The library-fit reading with a machine-findable subset, and the bound is the locator's bound in a
new place.** A library hint fails by generality — but a hint that asserts something ABOUT THE ITEM
makes a claim that is true of a carrier or is not.

**THREE FINDINGS, and the two classes are never added together.**

- `en-attribute-transfer` asserts A PAIR OF PEOPLE — **26 of 43 lack it, 4 LIVE.** CANDIDATE: rests
  on a name-counting proxy, named on the row.
- `en-negation-dropped` asserts A NEGATIVE — **4 of 36 lack it, 0 LIVE.** FINDABLE.
- `en-wrong-scope-retrieval` asserts LINE REFERENCES — **2 of 86 lack it, 1 LIVE.** FINDABLE, and
  small: this hint very nearly does fit.

**THE FIRST NEGATION NUMBER WAS 23 OF 36, AND IT WAS MANUFACTURED BY SCOPE.** The hint says *"find
the small negative word IN THE LINE"* — the word is in the TEXT, and I scanned the stem and options
only. **23 → 4, and 1 LIVE → 0.** R453 again: a wrong scope produces a real-looking count, and this
one was caught before it was reported rather than after.

**THE BOUND, AS A COUNT, ON EVERY RUN:** 5 English hints assert a feature this can test — the
population. 1 asserts something NOT SCREENED (a comparison is a technique reading; a list in an
option set is not a list in the text). **64 describe a MOVE and assert nothing about the item, so
there is nothing to test a carrier against** — unfindable, and that is the ordinary case rather than
a gap.

## R578 — Compliant by absence: a script that never completes is never wrong

**`export-cowork-workorder` sat on a fix list for four turns labelled UNTESTED, never staged.** The
label was treated as a pending task. **It was the symptom.**

`requirePopulation` was asserting that items NEED WORK, so **a clean bank aborted the export.** The
script had never once completed, and a script that never completes produces no artefact, fails no
downstream check, and appears in no fault list. **Its absence read as compliance for four turns.**

The repair is the population rule in its own instrument:

    SCREENED population  asserted NON-EMPTY — zero screened would mean a broken query.
    OUTPUT population    declared possibly-empty, WITH A REASON.
    DENOMINATOR          printed beside the empty output on every run.

**"0 items need work" and "nothing was examined" are the same line without the denominator** — which
is R60 exactly, arriving inside the guard that R60 built. `requirePopulation` does not know which of
an instrument's two populations it has been pointed at, and pointing it at the output rather than the
input converts a clean result into a crash.

**The transferable half: a never-run script is invisible to every check that reads OUTPUT.** Nothing
here screens for a script that always aborts, and 330 DRAFT items were being screened by nobody while
the fix list recorded the script as merely untested.

## R579 — The block solved a parsing problem; it does not solve a crossing problem

**Her line, and it is the entry: *a machine-readable record that nobody reads is a prose record with
extra formatting.*** The amendment block's own failure mode, arriving on the amendment block.

**THE DIAGNOSIS IS CROSSING, NOT READING, AND IT IS PROVED RATHER THAN INFERRED.** The reader parses
her sixty-seventh return's block, and reads **50 amendments from the indented BLOCK shape** across the
returns it can see. **`annie-sixtyfifth-return.md` is not on this disk.** The three wordings for
`WIW-10`, `WIW-12` and `WIW-13` were correctly formed and correctly parseable the whole time; the
file carrying them never arrived. **She is right to refuse to retype them into prose — typing them
again is the practice the block replaced.**

**AND THE GAP IS SEVEN, NOT THREE.** Returns **59, 60, 61, 63, 64, 65 and 66** have no file, each
sitting between two returns that do. `pnpm check:return-sequence` computes it from the ordinals in
the filenames — the same trick `check:register` has done for rule numbers since R1, never once
applied to **the channel the rules arrive through.**

**AN ABSENT RETURN IS NOT REPORTED ABSENT — IT IS NOT REPORTED.** Every reader here iterates the
files that are present, so a ruling in a return that did not cross is not late, it is invisible. That
is R568's null-from-a-renamed-field one level up: the shape of the evidence makes the missing thing
and the empty thing identical.

**A gap is reported, never repaired.** Only she can send a return, and only she can say whether a
number was ever used — an absent number may be a return that did not cross, or a ruling relayed in
conversation and never written to a file at all. **Both are the same fault from this side.**

**AND THE OUTBOUND LEG FAILED IDENTICALLY IN THE SAME TURN.** Batches three and four and the
attribute-transfer carriers are all in `from-cluecrew/` with their sidecars, staged at 14:09, 18:04
and 18:11. **Nothing new is on her disk.** R255 exactly — STAGED is not ARRIVED, and only the
receiver can report arrival — but this is the first time both directions have failed at once, which
is what makes it a channel fault rather than an incident.

## R580 — A description naming two branches, and a hint covering one
**Governed by R586 (assert or describe), which was stated after this and above it.**

**Two fields in one row, disagreeing, and nothing was comparing them.**

    en-attribute-transfer
      description: "Assigns one character's described attribute to another, OR THE RIGHT ATTRIBUTE
                    AT THE WRONG VALUE."
      childHint  : "Two people are being described. Check which one each detail belongs to."

**The second branch needs no second person**, and that is established from the two fields without a
single carrier being read.

**THIS IS NOT THE WIDENED-WITHOUT-HINT CHECK, and the difference is the whole reason it went
unseen.** Nothing here was widened. **The description was always broader than its hint**, from the
day both were written — so a change-detector cannot see it, because there was no change. 274 entries
were audited for drift with this sitting inside one of them.

**2 English findings from a findable population of 15**: `en-attribute-transfer`, and
`en-vocab-form-lookalike` — whose description names *a different word the target resembles* **or a
morpheme met in other words**, where the hint says only *"Read it letter by letter."* Letter-by-letter
reading does not reach a morpheme fault. 4 more in maths.

**THE BARE-`or` SPLITTER IS RECORDED AS REFUSED.** Allowing any ` or ` raised recall and destroyed
what the count is for: it split *"the spelling or punctuation error"* — one noun phrase — and it split
ACROSS SENTENCES, reporting `en-article-definiteness`'s trailing *"Distinct from en-a-an-by-spelling"*
note as an unaddressed branch. **Two of three English findings were the splitter, not the entry.**
Comma-or, first sentence only. Second bound refused this fortnight for the same reason as the locator's
three-word window: **a loose population with a stated size is worse than a tight one, because the size
is what the reader is trusting.**

## R581 — Failing systematically by question type is a different fault from failing at random
**Governed by R586 (assert or describe). Corrected by R585: the zeros are about the WORDING, never
the TAGGING — the entry applies to all four types.**

**`en-attribute-transfer` serves four question types and its wording belongs to one.**

    en-comp-inference   8 of 9 carriers have two named people
    en-comp-retrieval   9 of 23
    en-comp-technique   0 of 3
    en-comp-vocab       0 of 8

**On a vocabulary or technique item there are no characters at all**, so the hint does not merely
fail to help — it instructs an act the item does not contain. **A hint that misses a scattered few of
its carriers is slightly loose; a hint that fits every inference item and no vocabulary item was
written for one of the types its tag serves.** The first is repaired by rewording, the second by
scoping or splitting the entry. **A total cannot tell them apart, and the by-type counts are now
standing output rather than a one-off.**

**She authored it and did not miss it.** *"I wrote at the time that two people assumes exactly two,
considered widening it, and kept it… I was writing a hint for ninety-seven carriers I had not seen."*
**The fault is not inattention; it is authoring against an unseen population** — which is the argument
she has been putting to both stores all fortnight, arriving as an instance of itself.

**THE POPULATION FOR THE SAME SHAPE: 22 English entries whose carriers span two or more question
types.** A population, never a finding — a tag serving four types may still have one wording that
fits all four. Only the assert-a-feature subset is decided by looking.

## R582 — A check that cannot fail on a clean population, and one that cannot pass on one

**Hers, and it completes R578 from the other end.** *"A check must be able to fail by finding
nothing. This one could not pass by finding nothing."*

`export-cowork-workorder` asserted that items NEED WORK, so a clean bank aborted the export — it had
never once completed, and **compliant by absence** followed. The mirror of the rule this register has
been applying all fortnight to gates that see an empty population and report a pass.

**Both are one defect: a verdict fixed by the SIZE of a population rather than by its STATE.** A gate
that cannot fail on a clean bank and a gate that cannot pass on one are measuring the same wrong
thing. The repair is the same in both directions — assert the SCREENED population non-empty, declare
the OUTPUT population possibly-empty with a reason, and print the denominator beside it.

## R583 — 15 of 351: what "arrived" has actually rested on

**R255 said STAGED is not ARRIVED and only the receiver can report arrival. It never said how the
report would be RECOGNISED**, so arrival has been inferred from silence for a fortnight — the weakest
possible evidence, and **the same evidence a total channel failure produces.**

**She has been supplying the proof all along and nothing was reading it.** Her returns open with
*"Artefacts read, full digests computed here over the bytes"* and quote the filename and a sha256.
That is a receiver-side confirmation **over the actual bytes**, which is stronger than a delivery
receipt: it proves she read the same file that was staged, not merely that something was written.

`pnpm check:arrival-confirmed` joins the two sides. **351 staged artefacts; 24 distinct digests she
has quoted across 65 returns; 15 CONFIRMED.**

    CONFIRMED      15 — a return quotes a digest equal to this file's bytes.
    NOT CONFIRMED 336 — and this is NOT evidence of non-arrival. She confirms by digest only when
                        she opens a return with one, which is most turns she does not.
    UNMATCHED       9 — a digest in a return matching no staged file. She read something this store
                        cannot identify, and that direction had never been looked at.

**THE CHANNEL FAILED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS IN ONE TURN, and that is what makes it a channel fault rather
than an incident.** Seven returns absent by ordinal; three artefacts staged with sidecars at 14:09,
18:04 and 18:11 and nothing new on her disk. Each leg had a rule; neither had an instrument.

**What this cannot do: it reports UNCONFIRMED-arrival, never non-arrival, and they are not the same
claim.** Confirmation is a thing SHE does, so its absence is a fact about her returns and never about
the channel. **Silence is still silence. The change is that it is counted rather than read as
delivery.**

## R584 — The description-hint check is ONE-SIDED, and a clean run means nothing

**Hers.** A contradiction between the two fields is evidence. **Their agreement is evidence of
nothing, because both can be stale together** — which is precisely what the unlanded-amendment scope
correction showed: a description and a hint sitting in perfect accord, both wrong, with nothing in
the accord to say so.

So the check reports FAILURES and says, on a clean run and in the run's own output, that **a clean
run means nothing**. Otherwise the next reader takes seventy silent rows as seventy checked ones —
which is R60's fault arriving through the opposite door, an over-reading of a true zero rather than
an under-reporting of an empty one.

**A passing row is not a checked row.** The line prints whether or not anything is found, because the
reader who needs it most is the one who arrives on a green day.

## R585 — A zero by question type is a finding about the WORDING, never about the TAGGING

**She nearly over-called this and caught herself, and the correction is worth more than the finding.**

**Zero of eight vocabulary carriers signal two people — and the entry still applies to all eight.**
On `ENG-001-WIW-17`, asking what *grave* means in *'A grave round face'*, the option **"Dark and
dirty with earth"** gives the burial sense's attribute to a face. **That is attribute transfer
exactly, and there is no person in it.**

**The transfer is between THINGS. The hint was written as though it were between people.** So the
by-type zeros say the carriers lack the feature the HINT asserts; they do not say the entry is
misapplied, and a reader taking them that way would **retag correctly-tagged items** — repairing the
half that was right. The check now says so on the row that produces the zero.

## R586 — ASSERT OR DESCRIBE: the governing rule above R580 and R581

**Hers, and it is the rule those two entries are instances of.**

> **A hint that DESCRIBES A MOVE is true wherever the move is right. A hint that ASSERTS A FEATURE
> must be true of every carrier — and a library hint cannot see its carriers, so an assertion in one
> is a claim about a population its author cannot see. Prefer the move. Assert only where the
> assertion IS the teaching.**

*"Check which one each detail belongs to"* is a move, and it survives on all 43 carriers. *"Two people
are being described"* is an assertion, and it is false on 26 of them. **The same entry, the same
sentence, and the two halves have different truth conditions** — which is why the fault was invisible
to a reader checking whether the hint was good advice.

**And it names the pair.** The two ways she has got a hint wrong this week are:

- **instructing a channel not every child has** — *"Picture the word in print"*, which a child who
  cannot picture it cannot perform (R567);
- **asserting a feature not every carrier has** — *"Two people are being described"*, on an item
  about painting a house (R576).

**Both are a hint author writing against a population they cannot see**, from the two directions a
hint can face: outward to the child, and inward to the items. She stated the first about children a
fortnight before the second arrived about carriers, and did not connect them until both were on the
board.

## R587 — Both legs by digest: the gap becomes a list

**`check:manifest-diff` now runs both directions against a manifest, one parser for both.**

    OUTBOUND  her held manifest against what is staged here.
    INBOUND   her outputs manifest against what is on this disk.
              70 produced · 61 CROSSED · 9 NEVER ARRIVED · 0 digest-differs · 10 here-not-claimed.

**The nine, named rather than inferred:** returns 59, 60, 61, 63, 64, 65, 66, 68 — **and
`annie-merge-ack-and-gap-yard-note.md`, which is unnumbered.** The ordinal check could never have
found that one. **An ordinal gap finds numbered absences; a manifest finds absences.** Both were
needed and the cheaper one came first, which is the right order and not the same as sufficiency.

**THE FAILURE IS ENTIRELY IN THE CROSSING, and that is now established rather than assumed.** Her
side: 61 numbered returns, complete from the eighth to the sixty-eighth, no gaps, **all fifty
amendments correctly formed.** Nothing was unwritten, nothing misnumbered, no block malformed.

**THE FIRST SEVEN ARE NAMED FOR THEIR CLUSTER, NOT BY ORDINAL** — `eng003-set-a`, `eng003-second`
through `eng003-seventh`, `eng028`, the approval batch — which is why her count reads 61 rather than
68, and why `check:return-sequence` reports everything below 8 as UNKNOWN. **She has named the naming
as hers to fix so the check needs no special case**, which is the right repair: a special case in the
checker would make the inconsistency permanent and invisible.

**AND HER MANIFEST'S PROSE AND ITS OWN TABLE DISAGREE.** The prose names nine files as the first
seven; the table carries six of them. `annie-eng003-set-a-return.md`, `annie-eng028-return.md` and
`annie-approval-batch-return.md` are on this disk and not in her table. **R580 arriving in the
manifest that was written to close R579** — a description and a list, in one document, disagreeing.

## R588 — While the channel is down: rulings can be authored, writes should wait

**Hers, and it is proportionate rather than cautious.**

> **A ruling made on a stale picture is a ruling she can revisit. A write made on a stale ruling is a
> change to a store.**

The asymmetry is the whole argument: one is reversible by its author, the other is not reversible by
anyone without a second act.

**AND THE SIZE OF THE STALENESS IS KNOWN AND LARGE.** The eight returns that have not crossed contain
**the persona decline, four structural transcript rulings, twelve amendments and a re-prioritisation.**
**This store's last complete view of her is the fifty-eighth return.** Anything written against that
state is written against a picture missing all of it.

**Neither store knows by how much its picture of the other is frozen** — divergence accumulating in
both directions at once, invisibly, which is STAGED-versus-ARRIVED at its worst: not one file
missing, but two counterparts each reasoning about a version of the other that has moved.

## R589 — `en-vocab-form-lookalike` is a SPLIT, and the branch the hint cannot reach is the larger one

    description: "a DIFFERENT WORD the target resembles, or A MORPHEME she has met in other words"
    childHint  : "This word looks like one you know. Read it letter by letter…"

**Letter-by-letter reaches the first branch and cannot reach the second.** *Wont* against *won't* is
settled by reading the letters. **`stranger` read as `strange` + `er` is not: reading the letters
gives the same letters, and the fault is in how they were parsed.**

**Two branches, two moves — a SPLIT rather than a merged hint, by her own unstressed-vowel ruling: a
tag chooses one hint and one hint names one move.** She will not author either half without the
carriers, which is the rule she set herself last turn meeting its first test.

**20 carriers, 1 LIVE, all `en-comp-vocab`. The form signal: MORPHEME 13, LOOKALIKE 6, 1 unquoted —
so the branch her hint cannot reach is nearly two thirds of the population.**

**TWO SIGNAL DEFECTS, BOTH FOUND BY READING THE ROWS BEFORE SENDING THEM, AND BOTH MOVED THE COUNT.**

- **Prefixes were missing.** `misgave`, whose distractor is *"handed him something by mistake"*, is
  `mis-` + `gave` — a morpheme fault through and through, signalled LOOKALIKE because nothing looked
  at the front of the word.
- **The headword was the first quoted span, not the one the question asks about.** A vocabulary stem
  quotes the passage line AND the word; `ENG-002-pp-20` returned `". What does"` — a fragment.
  `tolerable` is `toler` + `-able`, and its distractor *"good at putting up with things"* is exactly
  that parse.

**MORPHEME 11 → 13.** A branch count is the thing she is about to author against, and a signal blind
to half the morphology would have handed her a smaller half than the corpus holds.

## R590 — Two widenings refused this fortnight, and nobody gets credit for a check they did not ship

**Hers, and it is about where the instinct runs.**

- The locator's **three-word-window** draft: more matches, and it would have searched hints that
  describe while the run printed *"unfindable where it describes"*.
- The description splitter's **bare `or`**: more findings, and two of three English ones were the
  splitter rather than the entry.

**Both would have raised the count and falsified a printed sentence.** Both were refused on the BOUND
rather than accepted on the recall.

**The instinct runs toward recall**, because a bigger number looks like a better check and a refused
widening leaves nothing behind to point at. **Nobody gets credit for a check they did not ship** —
which is exactly why it is worth writing down that it was refused, twice, and why.

## R591 — Language claiming a stronger population than the thing behind it

**Her strongest note, and it makes two of this week's faults one fault.**

    "the feature is present in EVERY carrier in en-comp-inference"    a report, where the test was 8 of 9
    "Two people are being described."                                 a hint, where 26 of 43 have none

**The first was corrected from *every* to *most* with the printed sentence changed to match. The
second is her own hint, and it asserted a population its author could not see.** One is a string in a
check and one is a string a child reads, and **they are the same defect: language whose scope is
wider than the thing standing behind it.**

It is R586 (assert or describe) turned on our own instruments rather than on the corpus. A check that
says *every* where it tested *most* is a hint that says *two people* where two thirds have one —
**and in both cases the wrong word is the one that makes the claim sound settled.**

**`en-vocab-form-lookalike` keeps its id, its hint and six carriers** — `rogue`/*rough*,
`covet`/*cover*, `wont`/*won't*, `sullen`/*sullied*, `stitch`, `order`. **Every one is a different
word the target resembles**, which is what the id says and what *read it letter by letter* reaches.

`stranger` as *strange* + *-er*, `misgave` as *mis* + *gave*, and ten more. **She has not mistaken
which word it is. She has taken it apart** — reading `stranger` letter by letter gives `stranger`,
because the letters were never the problem.

**`ENG-001-WIW-11` IS LEFT VISIBLY UNPLACED, and that is the entry's other half.** *Moving a boat
along with oars* for *the row* is a homograph — a different word with the same spelling, **neither a
resemblance nor a misparse.** It carries `unplacedBySplit` with her reasoning and her return's

it into whichever branch is nearest."*

**HER LISTS ARE THE AUTHORITY AND THE RESOLUTION IS ASSERTED.** The writer resolves each headword she
named to exactly one carrier and **fails the whole run** on any headword matching none or several, on
any carrier in neither list, and on any total other than 13 / 6 / 1. **A split that silently placed
twelve would look exactly like one that placed thirteen.** Read back after writing: 7 and 13.

population for four batches indistinguishable from a field nobody had looked at. **Only a recorded
decision separates them, and only a reader looking for one would find it.**

The delivery now excludes ruled rows and reports them in its denominators with the ruling verbatim.

## R595 — Memory in a manifest header, and a subset that looks like a population

**Two faults from opposite sides of the same week, and hers is the sharper.**

**SHE PUT RECOLLECTION IN THE HEADER OF A MANIFEST.** *"I generated that table from my own disk and
then wrote a header from memory of the sequence. The manifest exists to replace recollection with

**HER OWN CHECK WAS CORRECTLY SCOPED AND STILL REPORTED THE WRONG THING.** She reported her side

`annie-merge-ack-and-gap-yard-note.md` was invisible to it by construction.

somebody read the rows before sending them, and **the number alone would not have shown it.**

half and looks like a complete answer** — because **a subset of a real population is
indistinguishable from that population when you cannot see what was excluded.** Every row it returns

## R598 — Kind first, and the legacy branch says so on its face

**The canonical target syntax names WHAT KIND of thing it points at before WHICH one:**

    library:<entry-id>        item:<item-id>:<field>        word-card:<headword>        surface:<what>

**HER CENSUS IS THE CASE: 23 bare ids, 15 with a colon, 15 with a space, 1 parenthetical, 1 with no
id.** *"A field with three syntaxes is three fields wearing one name, and any parser must pick one
and be wrong about the others."* **It happened twice inside a single repair** (R594): the space form
was classified SURFACE and declared out of scope, then reported ABSENT while the store held it.

**THE ALREADY-WRITTEN TARGETS STAY AS THEY ARE.** Rewriting them would be a second wording under one
id, once per row — the exact fault the block exists to prevent. So the legacy syntaxes are parsed by
a branch that **says so on its face**, and `targetSyntaxCensus()` prints the split on every run:
canonical 15, legacy 46, no target 18. **A silent normaliser is how three syntaxes wearing one name
stayed invisible; a count on every run is the opposite of that.**

**AND THE TWO CENSUSES DIFFER BY EXACTLY THE CROSSING GAP.** This disk holds 18 bare / 15 colon /
8 space / 1 parenthetical against her 23 / 15 / 15 / 1. **The two categories that match exactly are
the ones the nine uncrossed returns do not touch**, and 5 + 7 + 1 is the thirteen amendments those
returns carry. The syntax census independently confirms the gap is transport and nothing else.

## R599 — A verdict that changes when the instrument is repaired is a fault in the INSTRUMENT

**It is only visible to somebody who RE-RUNS rather than stopping at the first fix.** A repair that

question that separates them is whether the underlying rows changed. **They had not.**

Sibling to R149 (baseline before changing an instrument) and R173 (the right answer for the wrong
reason), and sharper than both, because it needs no baseline and no suspicion — **only the discipline
of running the thing twice.**

## R600 — The unification half, above the refusal half, in her order

**Four amendments moved into service as a CONSEQUENCE of being applied**, not as a separate act.

in prose and the serving gate read fields.

**HER ORDER, AND IT IS THE POINT:**

    the REFUSAL half   stops unread text reaching a child.
    the UNIFICATION half stops read text failing to.

**She puts the second first.** The refusal half is the one everybody builds, because its failure is
visible and blameable — a child got something nobody checked. **The unification half fails silently
in the other direction**: work is done, approved, recorded, and never reaches anybody, and nothing
anywhere reports it. **Four returns of chasing is what that costs.**

## R601 — PU-08 generalised: a decision nothing reads is not a decision

**`hintServes: 'library'` was read by no code at all.** PU-08 served the library hint anyway — but
**only because its authorship fields happened to be absent. The decision and the outcome agreed by
accident.**

**And the accident was one amendment from breaking.** Applying an amendment sets both authorship
fields — that is R600, and it is how four hints moved into service this week. **Amend PU-08's wording
without noticing, and her ruling to withhold it is silently overturned by the act of improving the
text she ruled against serving.** `chooseHint` now honours an explicit ruling above the authorship
fields, says WHY, and a test asserts the ruling survives amendment.

**THE GENERAL SHAPE IS MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE.** `pnpm check:decision-visible` enumerates the
decision-bearing keys actually present in the store and asks whether any code reads them.
**2 READ, 9 UNREAD.**

**UNREAD IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A FAULT and the check never says it is.** Provenance is SUPPOSED to be
inert — nothing should branch on `hintAuthority`. **The fault is a field a human treats as a DECISION
while the system treats it as a comment**, and separating those two is a reading. The check names the
classes and reports its own bound: it matches the key NAME as a literal, so a computed key reads as
UNREAD, and UNREAD is a candidate list rather than a verdict.

## R602 — The delivery door deleted the batches it had just staged

**She reported batches three and four as never arriving. They arrived, and this door removed them.**

`deliver(path, family)` prunes superseded copies by prefix: `existing.startsWith(`${family}-`)`. With
family `unread-item-hints-for-annie`, **every `unread-item-hints-for-annie-batch-N-<hash>.json`
matches**, so the next delivery of the unbatched file deleted all four batches out of her directory —
printing `superseded → removed stale` each time, which is exactly what a correct supersede looks
like.

**A BATCH IS NOT AN OLDER VERSION OF THE WHOLE. It is a different slice of the same population**, and
the two are indistinguishable to a prefix test. The repair: the segment after `family-` must BE a
content hash, which a superseded version always has and a batch name never has in that position.

**AND THIS IS WHY THE OUTBOUND LEG LOOKED LIKE TRANSPORT.** Nine returns genuinely did not cross —
that is transport. **The batches were a mechanism fault on this side**, and both directions failing
at once made one look like the other. The manifest diff separated them: it costs one run, and it
corrected a working figure rather than a record, which is its first such use.

**The bound is printed: only rulings expressible as a property of a string are here.** Whether a
label is useful, or names the right group, is a reading. A clean run says these five hold and nothing
more.

## R604 — A field is a decision if it can be disobeyed

**Her criterion, and it sorted nine undifferentiated rows into the shape she predicted.**

    RECORD     a name, a date, a digest, a method. States what happened. Nothing can defy it, so
               nothing reading it is CORRECT — inertness is its right state.
    DECISION   an imperative or an evaluation. Says what SHOULD happen, so code can obey or ignore
               it, and a decision nothing reads is being ignored by default.
    AMBIGUOUS  neither shape settles it. **These go to her rather than being ruled here.**

**1 DECISION, 2 AMBIGUOUS, 4 RECORD** — she expected two or three ambiguous, not nine.

- **DECISION: `unplacedBySplit`.** Written by the split this turn, read by nothing. **A decision
  field created in the same turn as the check for that fault**, which is the fault demonstrating its
  own ordinariness.
- **AMBIGUOUS, hers: `approvedNotByRecognition` (7 rows), `hintRuling` (1).**

**A THIRD STATE WAS BUILT AND REMOVED, and the removal belongs here.** "REACHES A REVIEWER ONLY"
looked right for a decision about review rather than serving. **It cannot be computed**: a grep for
the key in `scripts/` matches the script that WRITES the field and the check that INSPECTS it as
readily as one that reads it, so the new class absorbed all seven rows including the four pure
records and the sort emptied. **A distinction the instrument cannot make is worse than the bound it
replaces**, because the bound is honest about what it does not know.

## R605 — Do not test the outcome. Ask what reads the field.

**`hintServes` was honoured for six weeks by accident.**

The outcome was correct on every run: PU-08 served the library hint exactly as she ruled. It did so
because its authorship fields were absent, **not because anything read the field carrying her
ruling.** No test of behaviour could have found it — the behaviour was right.

**A decision honoured by accident and a decision honoured by design are indistinguishable from the
output, and distinguishable in one grep.**

**AND THIS IS WHERE THE EXISTING ENTRY LANDS.** *A rule in the register is not a rule in the code
until something calls it* — arriving here **on a decision FIELD rather than on a rule**, which is the
more dangerous of the two. **A register entry looks like prose and invites the question "is this
enforced?". A field looks like state and does not.** `hintRuledBy: "Annie"` reads as settled.

**A decision recorded in a field nothing reads is a note that happens to be true.**

## R606 — The house-form count reconciles as two populations, one unnamed

**Her strict count is 11 of 36 and her inclusive count is 16. In the PR series strict gives 8 of 12 —
which is this proxy, to the row.**

**There was never a disagreement.** Two counts over different sets, and the set was not named on
either. Thirteen was neither figure; it was a third set nobody had stated.

**AND IT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR HAVING REFUSED TO WIDEN.** A detector stretched until it reached
thirteen would have fitted itself to a number that was not a measurement of anything — and it would
then have agreed, which is the camouflage R173 names. **The proxy agreed with her strict count on the
one series where both were computed, and it agreed because neither had been adjusted to the other.**

## R607 — The library reading is two passes, and assertion goes first

> **Generality is the failure this KIND is exposed to. Assertion is the failure it HAS.**

A library hint cannot see its carriers, so **breadth is its standing risk** — a wording wide enough
to fit everything. But a clause claiming a feature of the item is **either true of every carrier or
false on some**, and that is decidable rather than a matter of taste. **The comparison goes before
the judgement**, so the brief was rewritten: `theAssertingClauses` first, generality second.

**A clause is a MOVE if it is an imperative or a question. Anything else is an ASSERTION.**
`en-attribute-transfer` carries one of each in one sentence: *"Check which one each detail belongs
to"* survives all 43 carriers; *"Two people are being described"* is false on 26.

**41 of 53 English library hints carry an asserting clause. 15 assert something ABOUT THE ITEM**, and
those are the decidable ones — *"This one is in the lines"* (174 carriers), *"Some options just copy
words from the passage"* (115), *"Two people are being described"* (43). **The rest are general
truths**: *"Sounding sensible is not enough"* holds wherever the entry lands and cannot be false on a
carrier.

**THE CLAUSE IS MARKED ON EVERY ROW — the shape that made the visual-act file readable** (R569).
And the detector OVER-reports by design: a clause opening with a verb the imperative list does not
hold reads as an assertion, so **a false positive is a row to skim rather than a fault to miss.**

**Four of five amendments in one batch of nine is not a rate. It is a signal**, and this is the
measurement it asked for.

## R608 — Two fields carrying one decision present as two ambiguous fields

**Hers, and it names a fault neither field's kind could explain.** `hintRuling` and `hintServes` were
written as a pair; the classifier could sort neither, because **one decision split across two fields
looks like two half-decisions.**

    hintServes   THE DIRECTIVE. The only field that changes what a child receives.
    hintRuling   ITS REASON, in her words. Nothing branches on it and nothing should.
    hintRuledBy  who ruled.

**The fault was the split, not either field's kind.** Declared in `HintSource` so the next reader
meets the subordination where the field is defined rather than inferring it from behaviour.

**And `approvedNotByRecognition` is a RECORD: nothing can defy it.** With both ruled, **AMBIGUOUS is
0** — the class exists to carry what must reach her, and it is empty because she emptied it.

**One DECISION remains unread: `unplacedBySplit`**, written by the split and acted on by nothing. It
reaches a reviewer through the carrier delivery and never through the product, which is correct for a
decision about review — but the check cannot compute that distinction (R604) and reports it as
ignored. **Named here rather than fixed by a class the instrument cannot support.**

## R612 — The structural test: a library hint points at what the error guarantees

**Hers, and it is the REPAIR where R607 was the diagnosis.**

> **A library hint may point only at something that exists BY DEFINITION on every carrier of that
> error.** Ask of each entry: what does this error GUARANTEE is present? That is what the
> replacement points at. **Where nothing is guaranteed, the hint names a move and asserts nothing.**

**`en-extreme-option-pull` is the model**: *"Does the passage really go that far? Check the strongest
word in the option."* The error IS choosing an overreaching option, so a strongest word exists on
every carrier **by the definition of the error** — the hint cannot be false anywhere its tag is
right. *"Two people are being described"* points at a fact about the PASSAGE, which the error
guarantees nothing about. **The difference between the two is not care or quality; it is what the
assertion is anchored to.**

In the brief as `theStructuralTest`, applied to the fifteen aboutThisItem rows.

## R613 — The authoring position: the entry above the eight instances

**The fault in the failing library hints is not carelessness and not generality.** It is that **a
library hint is written while looking at ONE carrier** — the first, usually — **and no amount of care
fixes it, because the author cannot see the carriers that do not exist yet.**

She said it of herself (R581): *"I was writing a hint for ninety-seven carriers I had not seen."*
The structural test (R612) is the escape: **what the error guarantees is knowable WITHOUT seeing the
carriers**, because it follows from the error's definition rather than from any instance. An author
who anchors to the guarantee is immune to the position; an author who anchors to the carrier in front
of them writes `two people` because the carrier in front of them had two people.

**AND THE SAME TURN PRODUCED A NEW INSTANCE OF THE CLASS `check:reissue-completion` EXISTS FOR.**
`en-contraction-apostrophe` was approved in the eng003-third return — *"approved as written…
CZ-B7 D retags on its write; the row becomes servable when the entry lands"* — **and the entry never
landed.** The draft sat on disk, the approval sat in the return, and CZ-B7's `Youre` sat under
`en-apostrophe-possession`, whose hint's third sentence — *"Try swapping in 'it is'"* — does nothing
for *you're*. **Retagged on the entry's write, weeks late, as her original ruling specified.
Amending the possession hint to cover it would have fixed the symptom, kept the fault, and broken
the hint for the possessive carriers it fits** — R607's assertion fault manufactured on purpose.

**Her point: `en-vocab-neighbouring-sense`'s hint asserts a property of the WORD — *"More than one
meaning fits this word"* — so it is only true WHILE THE TAGGING IS RIGHT.** A mistag under most
entries gets an irrelevant move; **a mistag here gets a false assertion about the child's own word**,
told to a child who is holding a one-sense word and being sent to choose among its meanings.

`neighbouring-sense-carriers-38c7216fa1a86585.json`: **29 carriers, 4 LIVE, 0 without a quoted
headword** — each row naming the word, the key sense, and **the second sense the tag claims**, so a
